recipes.title: Easy Tikka Meatball Curry

items: 500 g meatballs (beef, chicken, lamb or pork)
400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan/frypan over medium heat.
Add meatballs and cook for 5 minutes until browned. Remove from pan.
Add onion to pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Spoon in curry paste, stir and cook for a further minute.
Add chickpeas, tomato purée and water. Stir well.
Place meatballs back into pan and bring to the boil. Turn temperature down and cover with lid. Simmer for 8–10 minutes or until meat is cooked through.
Pour coconut milk into pan, stirring gently. Cook for 2–3 minutes.
Serve with rice and vegetables.

notes: Serve with rice and vegetables.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken – Quick

items: 1/2 tsp each of ground ginger, cinnamon, salt and turmeric

steps.text: Mix spices together, then add chicken. Stir and set aside.
Melt butter in pan and sauté onion and garlic together for 2 minutes.
Add chicken and sauté for about 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cream/milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Can add veges along with the tomato paste, e.g. potato, pumpkin, frozen veg, spinach etc. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Quick Butter Chicken (Version 2)

items: 1/2 tsp each of ground ginger, cinnamon, salt and turmeric
3/4 cup cream (or milk with 2 tsp flour mixed in)

steps.text: Mix spices together, add chicken and put aside.
Melt butter in pan and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add chicken and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cream, turn down heat and simmer gently for 5 minutes.

notes: Can add vegetables to extend the meat. Can add chickpeas.

items: 2 Tbsp virgin coconut oil (or butter, ghee or other oil)
500 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into about 2 cm pieces
1 1/2 Tbsp garlic, finely grated (about 6 large cloves)
400 g full-fat coconut cream (or coconut milk)

ingredients.heading: To serve
items: Plain yoghurt, thinned with a little water

steps.text: Melt the coconut oil in a large pot over medium–high heat and cook the onion for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, then the curry powder, turmeric and cumin for 15 seconds (add a splash of water if it sticks).
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the chicken and coat it in the paste.
Add the stock and simmer rapidly for 5 minutes.
Add the coconut cream, chickpeas and salt and simmer rapidly for 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
Take off the heat and rest 5 minutes to thicken. Serve over rice with yoghurt and coriander, and naan if you like.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium–high heat. Cook the garlic, ginger and onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook until it turns white.
Add the curry powder and cook 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and stock, lower to medium and simmer rapidly for 10 minutes until thickened.
Add the peas and salt and cook 2 minutes more. Season and garnish with coriander.
Serve over rice, noodles or mashed potato.

items: 1 1/2 cups warm water (won't need it all)

steps.text: Finely chop onions and tomatoes. Cut potato into small cubes.
In a large pan/skillet, drizzle 3 Tbsp of oil and sauté the potato cubes over medium heat until golden brown. Remove from oil and set aside.
In the remaining oil, add the chopped onions and sauté them until translucent, then add the garlic and ginger. Stir for a few seconds and follow with tomato.
When the tomatoes become soft, add the tomato purée, salt, turmeric, garam masala, chilli powder/paprika and cumin. Stir well for 5 seconds, then follow with the ground beef and cook until brown.
Return potato to pan. Pour in some warm water, stir and simmer for another 8–10 minutes on low heat until beef and potato are cooked.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Chicken Curry (Dump Bag Option)

items: 1 large onion, peeled and finely chopped

steps.text: Put everything except garam masala into slow cooker and stir.
Put lid on and cook on High for 4 hours or Low for at least 6 hours.
When chicken is tender and falling apart, shred with 2 forks and stir in garam masala. Mix well.

notes: Dump bag prep – put everything except the garam masala in a freezer bag.

recipes.title: Vegetable Korma Curry

items: (or any combination of vegetables, e.g. cauliflower, zucchini etc.)

steps.text: Finely dice onion and cook in a frying pan for 5 minutes. Add finely chopped garlic and cook for another minute.
Put into slow cooker (or saucepan).
Peel and dice veges to about 1.5 cm dice. Place in slow cooker with the other ingredients and stir well.
Cook on high for 4–5 hours or low for 8–9 hours.

notes: Add a can of chickpeas for extra protein.

ingredients.heading: Seasoned chicken
items: 4 chicken thigh pieces, skin-on and bone-in (about 250 g each)

ingredients.heading: Curry
items: 2 Tbsp coconut oil (or other plain oil)
1 tsp pure chilli powder or cayenne pepper (reduce or omit to taste)
2 Tbsp lemon juice (or apple cider vinegar)
1/2 cup lightly packed coriander leaves (or parsley or baby spinach)
To serve: basmati rice and/or flatbreads or roti

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Brown the thighs skin side down for 4–5 minutes, turn for 1 minute, then remove. Brown the drumsticks on three sides (about 2 minutes each) and remove.
Turn to medium–high. Cook the onion 1 minute, the garlic and ginger 30 seconds, then the spices 30 seconds.
Stir in the coconut milk, tomato and salt. Return the chicken and juices, pushing it under the sauce.
Once simmering, lower to a gentle bubble. Cover for 10 minutes, then uncover and simmer 20 minutes more, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the lemon juice and half the coriander. Serve over rice, topped with the remaining coriander.

items: 1 1/2–2 cups beef broth (or 1 beef stock cube in 1 1/2 cups hot water)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a small pot and cook the beef until browned and the fat has rendered. Spoon off excess oil if you like.
Push the beef aside and cook the garlic, onion and ginger until soft. Stir in the carrot and potato, then add the broth, Worcestershire sauce and ketchup and bring to the boil.
Lower the heat, break in the curry roux and stir gently until dissolved. Simmer over medium heat for about 20 minutes until the vegetables are cooked, stirring occasionally.
If it tastes too salty, add hot water 1/4 cup at a time.
Serve with rice and soft-boiled eggs, topped with green onion.

items: 1.5 kg lamb shanks (5 small, 4 medium or 2–3 large)
114 g massaman curry paste (Maesri or Ayam)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).
Mix curry paste, coconut milk and stock in a 22 x 33 cm (9 x 13 inch) baking dish, preferably glass or ceramic. Add onion, potatoes, star anise, cinnamon and lamb.
Turn shanks to coat in sauce, then cover with foil.

Bake in oven for 2 hours. Remove foil, bake for a further 1 hour (small shanks) or 1.5 hours (medium–large shanks), turning lamb twice to brown evenly, until meat is so tender it can easily be teased apart with 2 forks.
Remove lamb onto a plate. Carefully skim excess fat off the surface. Mix sauce in baking dish – it should be reduced down to a syrupy thickness.
Serve lamb with sauce over rice.

items: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, quartered/large chunks
1 bottle Marion's Kitchen Sticky Chilli Ginger Marinade
2 long red chillies OR capsicum, finely sliced
Lime wedges and steamed rice, to serve

steps.text: Place the chicken in a bowl. Add 2 Tbsp of marinade and toss to combine.

Heat the oil in a large wok over high heat. Add the chicken and spread the pieces out. Allow to sear for 2 minutes or until golden brown on the first side. Then stir-fry and flip the chicken over. Sear for another 2–3 minutes to allow more colour to develop (add capsicum here).

Now add the coconut milk and remaining marinade to the wok. Stir through the fish sauce. Slowly bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring every so often, or until chicken is cooked through.
Stir through the basil and red chillies. Serve with steamed rice and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Beef Rendang (Singapore Family-Style)

items: 1/4 cup (60 ml) vegetable oil or coconut oil
2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into 5–7 cm pieces, or 3 kg beef short ribs
3 lemongrass stems, fat white stalks only, bruised
3 kaffir lime leaves, plus extra shredded lime leaves to garnish

ingredients.heading: Rempah (spice paste)
items: 2–6 bird's eye chillies (to taste), stalks removed

steps.text: Rempah: peel and roughly chop the onions, turmeric, galangal and ginger. Blend with the garlic and chillies to a purée, adding a splash of water if needed.

Heat the oil in a large heavy-based flameproof casserole over medium heat. Fry the rempah for 15–30 minutes – stir now and then at first, then constantly as it thickens so it doesn't catch – until browned, fragrant and thick.

Add the beef and coat it in the paste. Add the coconut cream and enough water to just cover the meat, then the lemongrass, whole lime leaves, cassia, star anise, sugar and salt. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for about 2 hours, until the beef starts to become tender.
Uncover and simmer for about 1 hour more, until the liquid has reduced to a thick, oily sauce.
Meanwhile, toast the coconut in a dry frying pan over medium–low heat, stirring constantly, for about 5 minutes until deep golden brown (this is kerisik).
Stir the kerisik into the rendang and simmer for about 30 minutes more, until deep brown, oily and thick.
Serve scattered with shredded lime leaves. It's even better made a day ahead so the flavours develop.

notes: A rendang is defined more by its fragrant rempah and thick coconut gravy than by hard spices.

items: 1 kg beef (such as chuck or round steak), cut into 2 cm cubes
2 large red chillies, seeds removed, sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep-sided frying pan over medium–high heat. Brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes each.
Return all the beef with the curry paste and fry for 1 minute. Add the lime leaves, star anise, coconut cream, water and sugar.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer on low for 3 hours, until the beef is tender and coated in a thick gravy with little liquid left.
Remove the star anise and lime leaves and serve garnished with the chilli.

recipes.title: Dry Bak Kut Teh (Malaysian Pork Stew)

items: 5 medium spring onions, white part chopped, green parts cut into 3 cm lengths
800 g pork belly, cut into bite-size chunks
12 large okra, cut into quarters diagonally

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium–high heat. Fry the garlic, ginger and chopped white spring onion for 1 minute.
Brown the pork in batches for about 3 minutes, then remove. Add the remaining oil with the sambal and dried chillies (if using) and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the okra and fry 2 minutes more.
Return the pork, add the green spring onion and stir in the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar.
Pour in the water or stock and bring to the boil. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Season to taste and serve hot.

items: 2 Tbsp lemongrass, finely chopped (finely shred some greener parts to garnish)
1.2 kg pork belly, cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium–high heat. Fry the shallots, garlic, ginger and lemongrass for 2 minutes.
Add the pork and fry for 10 minutes until browned. Add the hoisin, fish sauce, soy sauce and 1 cup water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.

In a small saucepan, bring the sugar and 3 Tbsp water to the boil. Simmer strongly, stirring constantly, for about 10 minutes until it caramelises to a dark golden brown. Very carefully pour it over the pork and stir through.
Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 1 hour, stirring every 10 minutes.
Season and serve garnished with shredded lemongrass, with rice if you like.

items: 1 kg skinless pork shoulder (or belly), cut into 6 cm cubes
1 large onion, halved, then cut into 8 mm wedges

ingredients.heading: Optional pineapple
items: 6 canned pineapple rings (in juice), each cut into 8, or 2 cups fresh pineapple pieces
To serve: 1 green onion, finely sliced; jasmine rice

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat and sear the pork in two batches until golden, about 4 minutes each. Set aside.
Lower to medium. Cook the onion for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the water, both soy sauces, vinegar, sugar, peppercorns and bay leaves, then return the pork and juices.
Bring to the boil, partly cover (leave a 2 cm gap) and simmer very gently on low for 1 1/2 hours, until fall-apart tender.
Meanwhile, if using pineapple, fry it in a non-stick pan over medium heat for about 4 minutes each side until golden.
Lift out the pork. Boil the sauce on high for 7–10 minutes until reduced to about 1 1/2 cups and lightly syrupy.
Turn to low, return the pork, pineapple and juices and stir gently to coat.
Serve over jasmine rice with green onion.

items: 1 kg pork shoulder, cut into 5 mm strips
2 small red capsicums, cut into 1.5 cm chunks

steps.text: Mix the olive oil, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and 1 tsp each of salt and pepper. Toss with the pork, cover and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Brown the pork in batches in a medium frying pan over medium heat, about 2 minutes per batch.
Put the pork in the slow cooker with the onion. Mix in all the remaining ingredients except the capsicum and cook on low for 6 hours.
Stir in the capsicum and cook 1 hour more.
Season and serve with rice or noodles, garnished with parsley.

items: 1.3 kg round or chuck steak, cut into 2.5 cm chunks
4 1/2 cups (1.25 L) chicken or mushroom stock

steps.text: Season the flour with salt and pepper and toss the beef in it with the cayenne until lightly coated.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large frying pan and brown the beef in batches, adding more oil as needed.
Whisk the lemon rind, ginger, mirin, tamari, rice wine and sugar.
Put the beef in the slow cooker, pour over the sauce, then add the stock.
Cook on high for 5 hours until tender.
Season and serve with the noodles, garnished with spring onion and coriander.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Beef and Vegetables

steps.text: Put sliced beef into a bag with half the oil and all other ingredients except the vegetables. Knead bag thoroughly to mix. Leave to stand for at least 15 minutes.
Select quick-cooking vegetables: mushrooms, snow peas, broccoli, cauliflower, celery, cabbage, onions, spinach etc. Slice into strips.
Heat oil in frypan and cook meat quickly. Remove meat from pan.
Cook vegetables in pan, then once cooked, add meat back in.
Serve with rice or noodles.

notes: Can use chicken and chicken stock instead of beef and beef stock.

recipes.title: Sesame Beef Stir Fry

ingredients.heading: Stir fry
items: 1 lb (about 450 g) flank steak, thinly sliced
1 cup snow peas, sliced in half across
1–2 Tbsp honey or light brown sugar

steps.text: Combine marinade ingredients in a bowl and add flank steak. Set aside for 15 minutes.

Heat 1 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large frypan over medium-high heat. Remove excess marinade from steak and cook in a single layer for 2–3 minutes, stirring to cook both sides. Depending on the size of your pan, you may need to do this in batches. Remove steak to a plate.
Heat remaining 1 Tbsp vegetable oil, then add peas, carrots and green onion and cook, stirring often, for 2–3 minutes.

Whisk together broth, soy sauce, honey/brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, sesame oil, fresh ginger, cornstarch and red pepper flakes. Add steak and sauce to frypan, stirring to combine. Sauce will thicken.
Stir in cooked ramen noodles if using, and serve.

notes: Serve with ramen noodles or rice.

items: 1 capsicum or 2 dried red chillies (sliced/roughly chopped)
1 Tbsp cornflour mixed with 1 Tbsp water

steps.text: Cutting against the grain, slice the flank steak into thin strips.
Combine the steak with the marinade ingredients. Mix well.
Combine the ingredients for the stir-fry sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok or frying pan over high heat. Add the beef and cook, stir-frying, for about 2 minutes or until just cooked. Transfer beef to a large tray or plate.

Return the same pan to the heat (no need to clean it). Add in the onion (plus a little more oil if required), capsicum/chillies, ginger and garlic. Stir-fry for about a minute, then add the stir-fry sauce. Allow to simmer for half a minute. Then add the cornflour mixture and simmer until thickened. Add the beef back into the sauce along with the spring onion and toss until well combined.
Serve warm, with rice.

items: 800 g porterhouse or sirloin steak, cut into strips
2 small spring onions, sliced, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Toss the beef with the cornflour and a good grind of salt and pepper.
Heat half the peanut and sesame oils in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef in batches for 3 minutes until browned, adding more oil as needed. Remove.
Add the ginger, garlic and five-spice and fry for 30 seconds, then add the remaining ingredients and bring to the boil.
Return the beef and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season and serve hot, garnished with spring onion.

items: 800 g porterhouse or sirloin steak, cut into thin, 3 cm long strips
2 large capsicums (preferably red and green), chopped into 1.5 cm cubes
1 large orange, rind finely grated (1 1/2 Tbsp) and juiced
1 cup (250 ml) chicken or vegetable stock

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef in batches for 3 minutes each until browned, adding oil as needed. Remove.
Add any remaining oil and stir-fry the capsicum for 2 minutes, then remove.

Fry the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then add the orange rind, sugar, soy sauce and chilli sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute. Stir in 1/2 cup of the orange juice and the stock, bring to the boil, then turn to low.
Mix the cornflour with the water and stir in. Bring back to the boil, stirring constantly, then return the beef and capsicum and heat through.
Season with any remaining orange juice and extra chilli sauce. Serve with steamed rice.

items: 900 g sirloin steak, cut into fine strips
3 Tbsp fresh chives, chopped, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Whisk the garlic, gochujang, brown sugar, peanut oil, chilli sauce, rice wine and tamari. Mix well with the beef in a large sealable container, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Heat a large wok over medium–high heat. Mix the onion and carrot through the beef, then stir-fry in batches for about 4 minutes until the beef is cooked through.
Serve hot, sprinkled with sesame seeds and chives.

items: 3 garlic cloves, roughly chopped (or prefer minced/sliced)

steps.text: Slice chicken against the grain on the diagonal into wide strips no more than 3–4 mm thick.
Whisk together the marinade ingredients in a large bowl. Add the chicken and mix well. Set aside for 10 minutes.
Mix hoisin stir-fry sauce ingredients in a small bowl.

Heat vegetable oil in a wok/large frying pan over high heat. Add onion and stir-fry for 30 seconds until just starting to char. Push onion to the sides of the pan and add the chicken and marinade into the centre. Spread out the chicken and leave for about 3–4 minutes or until a crust begins to form. Then combine with other ingredients in the pan.

Toss through garlic, then add the capsicum. Stir-fry for another 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the stir-fry sauce (pouring it around the edge of the pan) and stir-fry for another 30 seconds, or until everything is well coated, the sauce has thickened slightly and the chicken is just cooked. Toss through the spring onion. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chop Suey – Chicken Stir Fry
introNotes: This is for 2–3 servings; adjust as required. Serve with rice. The sauce is a light flavour, so adjust as desired.

steps.text: Velvet chicken (optional): place chicken in a bowl, sprinkle over baking soda and mix well. Set aside for 20 minutes (no longer than 30 minutes). Rinse well, and pat excess water with paper towels. Set aside.
Prep sauce: place cornflour and soy sauce in a bowl. Mix until lump-free, then add remaining sauce ingredients and stir.
Chop choy sum: trim end off choy sum and cut into 7 cm pieces. Separate stems from leaves.
Chop carrot: peel, then cut into 3 cm pieces and slice thinly.
Stir fry: heat oil in a wok/skillet over high heat. Add garlic, stir quickly, then add onion. Cook for 1 minute, moving constantly, until onion starts to wilt.
Add chicken and cook for 1 minute until the surface changes from pink to white.
Add choy sum stems, carrot and mushrooms. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add choy sum leaves, beansprouts and sauce. Stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens to a thick syrup consistency. Vegetables should still be tender-crisp, not soggy and soft.
Serve immediately with rice.

notes: Cooking times might be slightly longer than stated, depending on how hot your pan is.

items: 800 g skinless chicken thigh fillets, cut into bite-size chunks
3 large assorted capsicums, cut into 1 cm chunks

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the garlic, sugar, five-spice, soy sauce and mirin. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Heat the sesame oil in a large wok over medium–high heat. Stir-fry the cashews for 2 minutes until starting to brown, then remove.
Add the vegetable oil and heat until smoking. Stir-fry the chicken in batches for 6 minutes until cooked through, then remove.
Stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the capsicum and chilli and cook 3 minutes.
Return the chicken with the oyster sauce and 2 Tbsp water. Mix the cornflour with 3 Tbsp water, add and stir for 1 minute.
Return the cashews and heat through for 1 minute. Season and serve hot.

items: 800 g chicken breasts, skin off, cut into 1.5 cm chunks

steps.text: In a large bowl, mix 1 tsp of the soy sauce with the cornflour, then toss with the chicken.
Mix the stock, remaining soy sauce, rice wine, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil and set aside.
Heat the peanut oil in a large wok over high heat. Add the chilli sauce, garlic, ginger and chicken and stir-fry for 6 minutes. Add the celery and stir-fry 2 minutes more.
Add the soy mixture and cook until it thickens to a sauce.
Stir through the peanuts and serve hot.

items: 1 bunch gai lan (Chinese broccoli), cut into 3 cm diagonal slices
2 large red chillies, seeds removed, thinly sliced
1/3 cup (5 g) fresh Thai basil leaves, roughly chopped

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large wok over medium–high heat. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the sugar and cook 30 seconds more.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 5 minutes. Add the gai lan and cook 2 minutes more.
Whisk the chilli, lime juice, soy sauce and fish sauce, pour over the pork and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the basil, season and serve hot.

recipes.title: Speedy Pork Satay San Choy Bau

steps.text: Place noodles in a heatproof bowl. Cover with boiling water and set aside for 5 minutes to soften. Drain.
Meanwhile, combine soy sauce, peanut butter and 1/2 cup (125 ml) water in a small bowl.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the mince and cook, stirring with a wooden spoon to break up the lumps, for 6 minutes or until the mince changes colour. Add the ginger, garlic and spring onion and stir-fry for 1 minute or until aromatic. Add broccoli and soy sauce mixture and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes or until the sauce thickens. Stir in the vinegar.
Divide the lettuce among serving plates. Top with the noodles and mince mixture. Sprinkle with peanuts to serve.
Heat half the oil in a large wok over high heat. Stir-fry the celery and onion for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the remaining oil, the mince and spring onion and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Mix the oyster sauce, sweet chilli sauce and tamari, pour over the mince and stir through for 2 minutes. Season to taste.
Serve with lettuce leaves on the side to use as wraps.

recipes.title: Japchae – Korean Glass Noodle Stir Fry
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

items: 170 g flank steak, cut into thin strips
4 fresh shiitake mushrooms, cut into thin strips
1 small red capsicum, cut into thin strips
3 scallions (green onion), cut into 3-inch sections and thinly sliced

steps.text: Mix the beef together with 1 clove of garlic, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, 1 Tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp sesame oil.

Prepare the vegetables and set aside. Cook the noodles according to packet instructions. Strain and cut with scissors so that they're a little shorter. Add 1 Tbsp sesame oil, 1 Tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp sugar to the noodles. Toss thoroughly.

Heat up a frypan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the onion and carrot with 1 Tbsp vegetable oil until tender but still a little crunchy. Transfer to a large mixing bowl. Add another tablespoon of oil to the pan and add the mushrooms. Cook until caramelised and transfer to the mixing bowl with the onion and carrot. Add another tablespoon of oil to the pan and cook the red capsicum until tender. Add in the spinach, scallions and the remaining garlic. Cook the entire mixture until the scallions and spinach are wilted. Transfer to the mixing bowl with the other vegetables.
Turn up your heat to high and add beef to the pan. Stir-fry for a couple of minutes until the beef is no longer pink. Transfer the noodles and beef to the mixing bowl, along with the sesame seeds.
Add 3 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, 2 1/2 Tbsp soy sauce and 1 Tbsp sesame oil to the mixing bowl full of ingredients. Toss to combine all the ingredients together, and serve.

recipes.title: Japanese-Style Pork and Soba Noodle Stir-Fry

items: 500 g pork sirloin steaks, trimmed and thinly sliced
350 g packet Australian Superfood Vegetable Mix (Coles)

steps.text: Cook the noodles in a large saucepan of boiling water following packet directions or until just tender. Refresh under cold water. Drain well.
Meanwhile, heat half the oil in a wok or large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the pork, in 2 batches, for 3–4 minutes or until just cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Heat the remaining oil in the wok or pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes or until the onion softens. Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 1 minute.

Add teriyaki marinade, soy sauce and vinegar to wok or pan. Stir-fry for 1 minute. Add vegetable mix. Stir-fry for 1 minute or until heated through. Return pork to wok or pan with noodles. Toss for 1–2 minutes or until combined and heated through.

recipes.title: Yaki Udon
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life
introNotes: Replace the pork with chicken/beef/tofu, and use vegetables you have on hand.

items: 450 g frozen udon noodles or 200 g dry udon noodles
2 tsp dashi powder (or chicken stock powder)

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. If using frozen udon noodles, add the noodles and boil for 30 seconds–1 minute to loosen them. If using dried noodles, cook according to package instructions. Drain, rinse in cold water to remove excess starch, and drain thoroughly again. Set aside.

Place a large Dutch oven, non-stick pot or large cast iron skillet over medium heat. When the pan is heated, add the butter. Once partially melted, stir in the garlic and dashi granules. Cook for 30 seconds, until the dashi partially dissolves. At this point, the butter should be a light brown colour.
Add the drained noodles and toss to coat them in the butter. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat, until the noodles have dried out and are slightly crisped. Remove and set aside.
Add a tablespoon of oil to the pot, along with the pork shoulder. Brown the pork until crisp on the edges. Add the mushrooms and mirin, and cook until caramelised.
Add the cabbage, carrot, pepper, soy sauce and water. Stir-fry until the vegetables are wilted, and add the noodles back in, along with the scallions. Stir-fry for another minute. Serve!

recipes.title: Chicken Pan-Fried Noodles (Gai See Chow Mein)
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

ingredients.heading: Stir fry
items: 2 chicken breasts, cut into thin strips (can use equivalent thigh)
1 bunch choy sum/baby bok choy (2–3 cups, washed thoroughly)
4 bundles dried thin egg noodles (Hong Kong-style noodles)

steps.text: In a bowl, combine marinade ingredients with sliced chicken and set aside. Chop vegetables into manageable pieces and set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add dried noodles. Cook until they're just softened (do not overcook). Rinse with cold water, drain and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine sauce ingredients. In another bowl, mix slurry and set aside.

Heat wok/large skillet over high heat and add 2 Tbsp oil. Spread out your noodles in an even layer and fry for about 3 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Flip the noodles over and fry the other side (can add a bit more oil if necessary). When the noodles are golden on both sides, transfer the noodles to a large round plate.

Next, heat the wok until just smoking and add another tablespoon of oil. Sear the chicken. Once browned, add the garlic and then the Shaoxing wine to deglaze the pan. Pour in the sauce. Let the liquid come to a boil, and add your green vegetables. Stir and cook for about a minute.

Stir up your slurry again. Once liquid is boiling, add about 2/3 of the slurry and stir to thicken. Add more slurry until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Allow to bubble up for another 30 seconds.
Pour the entire mixture over the noodles and serve immediately.

items: 140 g dried ramen or noodle cakes
1 1/2 tsp Maggi seasoning (or 1 tsp extra soy sauce and 1/2 tsp Worcestershire)
Optional extras: fried/soft-boiled egg, dash of sesame oil

steps.text: Cook noodles per packet directions. Scoop out 1/2 cup cooking water. Strain noodles and set aside.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add garlic and cook, stirring, until soft. Add oyster sauce, soy sauce and Maggi seasoning with 1/4 cup cooking water. Stir to combine.

Add cooked noodles, parmesan and green onion. Toss until the noodles are all coated and the sauce is not pooled in the bottom of the pan. Add more cooking water, 1 Tbsp at a time, if needed to loosen the noodles.

items: 400 g baby prawns, shells and tails removed
2 cups (100 g) bean sprouts, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Cook both noodles following the packet directions. Drain and toss with 2 tsp oil so they don't stick.
Mix the oyster sauce, both soy sauces, water, brown sugar and fish sauce. Set aside.
Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large wok over high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 30 seconds, then remove.
Cook the sausage for 2 minutes, add the bean sprouts and cook 2 minutes more, then remove.
Add 1 Tbsp oil and turn the heat to medium. Pour in the egg and swirl to spread it evenly. Cook for 2 minutes, then scramble.
Return the prawns, sausage and sprouts, add the noodles and pour over the sauce. Toss for about 3 minutes until hot. Season and serve.

recipes.title: Easy Vegetable Chow Mein

items: 2 small red and green capsicums, halved and sliced
700 g Hokkien noodles, cooked following packet directions
2 cups (150 g) small broccoli florets (or other vegetable), optional

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat. Add the carrot, capsicum, mushrooms, garlic and broccoli (if using) and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Mix the oyster sauce, half the soy sauce and the rice vinegar, pour over the vegetables and cook 1 minute more.
Toss through the noodles.
Add more soy sauce to taste and serve hot.

notes: Works with most vegetables – a great end-of-week way to use up what's in the crisper.

items: 400 g fresh Chinese egg noodles, cooked
100 g Chinese broccoli (gai lan), blanched until tender

steps.text: Soak the mushrooms in the hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, keeping the soaking liquid.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium–high heat and stir-fry the ginger, garlic and spring onion for 1 minute.
Add the star anise, cinnamon, mushrooms and soaking liquid, Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, sugar and 750 ml water. Bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken and simmer 10 minutes, then turn off the heat, cover and leave the chicken to steep for 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and mushrooms. Season the braising liquid with salt.
Pour 60 ml braising liquid into each of four shallow bowls, add the noodles, then top with gai lan, sliced chicken and a mushroom.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve with sambal on the side.

items: 700 g beef brisket, cut into roughly 2 cm chunks
2 cups (200 g) red cabbage, finely sliced

ingredients.heading: Optional
items: 2 Tbsp mixed sesame seeds, to garnish
2 Tbsp fresh parsley, roughly chopped, to garnish

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and fry 5 minutes more until browned. Add the stock and bring to the boil.
Cover and simmer gently on low for at least 1 hour, until the beef is tender, adding more stock if needed.
Stir in the noodles and miso and simmer for 5 minutes until the noodles are cooked.
Season with tamari, salt and pepper. Serve topped with cabbage, radish, sesame seeds and parsley.
Put the eggs in a medium pot with at least 3 cm water over them. Bring to the boil, turn off the heat and leave them: 10–12 minutes for hard-boiled, 6–8 minutes for soft-boiled.
Bring the stock to the boil, reduce to a simmer and cook the noodles following the packet directions.
Blanch the zucchini and snow peas in a separate pot of lightly salted boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Divide the noodles and stock among bowls with the zucchini, snow peas, carrot and halved eggs. Drizzle with sesame oil, season, and garnish with marjoram and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Banh Canh (Thick Noodle Soup with Crispy Pork)

items: 3 small red chillies, finely sliced, to garnish

steps.text: Lightly season the flour and mix in the onion powder. Dip the pork steaks in the egg, let the excess drip off, then coat lightly in the flour.
Heat about 2 cm oil in a large deep-sided frying pan over high heat. Fry two steaks at a time for 5 minutes each side until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel, then cut into 1.5 cm slices.
Cook the noodles following the packet directions and divide among bowls.
Bring the stock to the boil, add the spring onion and simmer for 1 minute. Pour over the noodles, top with the pork and garnish with chilli and coriander.

recipes.title: Spicy, Sweet and Sour General Tso Chicken

items: 800 g skinless chicken thigh fillets, cut into 2 cm chunks
1/3 cup (40 g) plain flour, lightly seasoned
2 Tbsp fresh parsley, roughly chopped, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Whisk the stock, garlic, ginger, sambal oelek, chilli flakes, soy sauce, vinegar and paprika (if using). Set aside.

Bring the sugar and water to a light boil in a small saucepan, then simmer for 5 minutes until just turning golden – stir as little as possible. Add the stock mixture and bring to the boil, stirring constantly. Remove from the heat.
Toss the chicken in the flour until well coated.
Heat half the oil in a large wok over medium–high heat. Cook the chicken in batches, adding more oil as needed, and drain on paper towel.
Pour the sauce into the wok and bring to a simmer, then add the chicken and heat through.
Season and serve hot, garnished with parsley.

items: 800 g skinless chicken thigh fillets, cut into bite-size chunks
2 Tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying

steps.text: Toss the chicken with 1/2 tsp of the sesame oil, the soy sauce, 1/2 Tbsp water and the egg white.
Mix the salt, pepper, 3 Tbsp of the cornflour and the plain flour in a large bowl. Toss the chicken in it, pressing the floury clumps onto the pieces.
Heat at least 6 cm oil in a deep pot. Fry the chicken in small batches until golden brown and drain on paper towel.

Sauce: heat the remaining sesame oil and 2 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the chilli and garlic for 30 seconds, then add the vinegar, honey and stock and stir until almost boiling. Reduce to a simmer and season (it should taste quite sweet).
Mix the remaining cornflour with 3 Tbsp water, stir into the sauce until thickened, then gently fold through the chicken.
Serve hot, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Honey Sesame Chicken
recipes.source: Dinner at the Zoo (dinneratthezoo.com) – method summarised; converted to metric

ingredients.heading: Chicken
items: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 1/4 cup soy sauce (reduced salt if possible)

steps.text: Season the beaten eggs with salt and pepper. Mix the flour and 1/2 cup cornflour in a shallow dish.
Dip each chicken piece in egg, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat about 7.5 cm oil in a deep pan to 180 °C. Fry 7–8 pieces at a time for about 5 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Meanwhile, whisk the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, sugar, vinegar, sesame oil and 2 tsp cornflour.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the garlic 30 seconds. Add the sauce and simmer 3–4 minutes until just thickened.
Toss the chicken through the sauce, top with sesame seeds and green onion, and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Honey Chicken (Crispy Batter)
recipes.yield: Serves 4 as part of a shared meal

items: 500 g chicken breast, cut into long strips
1–2 L oil for deep-frying, plus a little for the wok
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, to serve

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the batter ingredients and rest for at least 15 minutes. Stir the honey sauce ingredients together.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan to about 175 °C. Fry the chicken in batches for about 5 minutes until cooked through. Raise the oil to 200 °C and fry again in batches until brown and crisp.
Heat a wok over high heat with a little oil. Add the honey sauce and simmer about 2 minutes until thick, then toss through the chicken.
Serve scattered with sesame seeds.

items: 600 g boneless chicken thigh fillets, preferably skin-on
1 cup loosely packed Thai basil leaves

steps.text: Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and marinate with the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar and five spice for at least 10 minutes. Toss in the sweet potato flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil to 150 °C. Fry the basil for about 20 seconds until crisp and translucent, then drain.
Raise the oil to 170 °C and fry the chicken in batches for about 3 minutes until golden, skimming out loose bits of flour.
Spiced salt: toast the salt and seasonings in a dry pan over low–medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Toss the chicken with the fried basil and a good pinch of spiced salt. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Triple-Fried Kara-age (Japanese Fried Chicken)
recipes.yield: Serves 4 as part of a shared meal | Prep 15 mins + 15 mins standing | Cook 15 mins

items: 3–4 boneless chicken thighs (about 600 g), skin on
1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger, juice only
3/4 cup (90 g) potato flour or cornflour
8 cups (2 L) rice bran, canola, sunflower or other vegetable oil, for deep-frying

steps.text: Cut the chicken into 5 cm pieces. Mix with the soy sauce, sake, ginger juice and sugar and leave for 10 minutes.

Put the flour on a tray. Using chopsticks, lift the chicken pieces out of the marinade one at a time and drop them into the flour (this stops excess marinade going in and the pieces sticking together). Shake off excess flour and lay on a tray in a single layer.
Leave the floured chicken uncovered for at least 5 minutes before frying.
Heat the oil to 180 °C in a wide saucepan.
Fry in batches, three times each: fry 1 minute, rest on a wire rack 30 seconds; fry 30 seconds, rest 30 seconds; then fry a final 30 seconds–1 minute and rest 2 minutes on the rack.
Serve with lemon slices and Japanese mayonnaise, with a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi if you like.

notes: The 5-minute rest after flouring lets the flour soak up the marinade and dry slightly – the secret to crisp, flavourful kara-age.

recipes.title: Korean-Style Sweet Chilli Fried Chicken Drumsticks

items: 1/2 cup (60 g) plain flour, lightly seasoned

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry, then coat lightly in flour, dip in egg and coat lightly in cornflour.
Heat 5 cm oil in a deep-sided saucepan and fry the chicken in small batches for 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on a wire rack over paper towel.
Warm the gochujang, sugar, tamari, sweet chilli sauce and vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve hot, scattered with dried chillies and almonds.

items: 800 g pork fillet, cut into bite-size chunks
1 green and 1 red capsicum, cut into cubes
1 x 400 g tin pineapple pieces, drained

steps.text: Toss the pork with the egg white and 1 tsp salt until well coated.
Mix 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 3 Tbsp of the cornflour and the plain flour in a large bowl. Toss the pork in it, pressing the floury clumps onto the pieces.
Heat at least 6 cm vegetable oil in a deep pot and fry the pork in small batches until golden. Drain on paper towel.

Heat the peanut oil in a large saucepan over medium–high heat. Fry the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the capsicum and pineapple and stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly soft. Add the vinegar, honey and stock and bring almost to the boil. Simmer and season (it should taste quite sweet).
Mix the remaining cornflour with the water, stir into the sauce until thick, then gently fold through the pork.
Serve on rice.

items: 1 kg pork shoulder, cut crosswise into 2 cm strips and patted dry

steps.text: Whisk the curry paste, stock powder, cornflour, fish sauce, flour and eggs in a large bowl.
Add the pork and coat well. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes – keep it as cold as possible until frying.
Heat at least 5 cm oil in a large pot over high heat. Fry the garlic slices for about 1 minute until golden, then drain on paper towel.
Fry the pork for about 8 minutes until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack over paper towel.
Cut into bite-size pieces and serve hot with the fried garlic and sesame seeds.

items: 4 x 200 g pork loin fillets, pounded to 2 cm thick
3 cups (300 g) finely shredded white cabbage
1/2 cup (60 g) plain flour, lightly seasoned

steps.text: Coat the pork in flour and shake off the excess, then dip in egg and press firmly into the breadcrumbs for a thick coating.
Heat about 2 cm oil in a large deep-sided frying pan over high heat. Fry two cutlets at a time for 5 minutes each side until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Slice the tonkatsu into 1 cm strips.
Mix the garlic, rice vinegar and sugar and toss through the cabbage.
Serve the pork with the cabbage and sweet chilli sauce, garnished with greens if using.

recipes.title: Asian Beef Bowls

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 1 Tbsp Chinese cooking wine or mirin

steps.text: Mix sauce together in a bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add garlic and onion and cook for 1 minute or until onion starts browning.
Add beef and cook, breaking it up as you go.

Once the beef has all changed from red to brown, add sauce. Cook for a further 2 minutes or until sauce has evaporated and beef is cooked. If you want the beef cooked more, add a splash of water and keep cooking (if desired).
Stir through shallots/scallions, then serve over rice, garnished with more shallots and sesame seeds if desired.

notes: Serve with rice or ramen noodles. Can add vegetables (e.g. carrot) or a shredded/julienned mixed vegetable packet (e.g. Superfood vegetable or beetroot slaw) in step 4.

recipes.title: Yoshinoya-Style Gyudon (Japanese Beef Rice Bowl)

items: 500 g beef scotch fillet, topside or rump, very thinly sliced
1 brown onion, peeled and thickly sliced
Benishouga (Japanese red pickled ginger), to serve (optional)
Shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven spice), to serve (optional)

steps.text: Combine the stock or dashi and teriyaki sauce with the sugar (if using) in a medium saucepan and bring to the boil.
Add in the onion and simmer for 2–3 minutes until the onion has softened.
Add in the beef and stir until the beef is just cooked. Season with salt if necessary.

Fill 4 bowls with rice, flattening the top of the rice, and then add the beef mixture on top, allowing a little of the stock to soak into the rice. Sprinkle over a little Japanese seven spice if you like, and serve with spring onion and pickled ginger.

notes: Can even serve with poached (soft-boiled) eggs.

recipes.title: Chicken Katsu Don
recipes.yield: Serves 2 | Prep 10 mins | Cook 30 mins | Total 40 mins

items: Salt (kosher or sea salt; use half if using table salt)
3 large eggs (1 for chicken katsu, 2 for donburi)
Neutral-flavoured oil (vegetable, canola etc.) for deep frying
Ichimi togarashi (Japanese chilli pepper), for garnish

steps.text: Gather all the ingredients. Dust salt and pepper on chicken tenders and dredge in the flour, the beaten egg (1 egg) and the panko.
Heat 1/2 inch of oil in a frying pan and deep fry at 180 °C until golden brown. Take out the chicken and drain extra oil on paper towel.
Slice onion and make dashi stock.
In a frying pan, bring seasonings and onion to a boil.
Lower the heat to medium and cook onion until wilted.
Put chicken katsu in and turn the heat up to medium-high. Pour and distribute the beaten egg (2 eggs) evenly.
When egg is half cooked, add mitsuba and turn off the heat.
Serve rice in a donburi bowl and put chicken and egg mixture on top. Serve with ichimi togarashi (chilli pepper) on the side.

recipes.title: Oyakodon (Chicken & Egg Rice Bowl)

items: 4 boneless free-range chicken thighs, skin on
2 cups (500 ml) bonito stock (preferably) or chicken stock
2 brown onions, cut into 1 cm slices

ingredients.heading: To serve
items: 8 cups (1.5 kg) warm, cooked short-grain rice
1 nori sheet, cut into 5 cm strips, then very finely sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the chicken, skin side down, for about 3 minutes until well browned (it doesn't need to be cooked through). Remove and cut into 5 cm pieces.
Add the stock, soy sauce, sake, mirin and sugar to the pan with the onion. Bring to a simmer, return the chicken and simmer for about 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to low and pour in the beaten egg. Give it only a few stirs with a wooden spoon, then cook for about 2 minutes until the egg just begins to set.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and slide a quarter of the chicken and egg on top of each. Finish with spring onion, nori shreds and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi.

notes: For extra flavour, skip the soy sauce, sake, mirin and sugar and use about 1/2 cup (125 ml) teriyaki glaze instead.

ingredients.heading: Korean beef and marinade
items: 250 g beef tenderloin or thick steak, very finely sliced
1/4 green apple, grated using a box grater

steps.text: Bibimbap sauce: mix all ingredients until sugar is dissolved.
Marinated beef: mix the marinade in a bowl, then add beef. Marinate for 30 minutes to overnight.

Heat 2 tsp oil in a large skillet over high heat. Let excess marinade drip off, then add beef. Cook for 3–4 minutes until cooked and there are some caramelised bits, then remove from skillet. Keep warm until required, or reheat to warm.
Prepare vegetables – shiitake: soak mushrooms in a large bowl of boiling water for 30 minutes, or until rehydrated. Drain, squeeze out excess water, then slice.

Carrot and zucchini salting (optional): place carrot and zucchini in separate bowls, sprinkle each with 1/4 tsp salt, toss, and leave for 20 minutes, then drain excess liquid. OR add salt when sautéing.
Cook vegetables – get 2 skillets going if you can.
Shiitake: heat 2 tsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook mushrooms for 2 minutes. Add 1 1/2 tsp soy sauce, 1/4 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp of garlic. Stir for 1 minute, then remove.
Carrot: add 2 tsp oil into the skillet and cook carrot until just tender (5–8 minutes), then remove.
Zucchini: cook as with carrot for 4 minutes.

Spinach: heat 2 tsp vegetable oil with a splash of sesame oil. Add spinach and sauté until starting to wilt. Add 1/2 tsp garlic and salt to taste, stir, then remove. When cool, squeeze to drain out excess liquid.

Beansprouts: simmer in water for 5 minutes, or steam in microwave for 3 minutes, until floppy. Drain under cold water, then cool. Squeeze out excess liquid with hands and place in bowl. Mix with 2 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp garlic and 1/4 tsp fish sauce.
Vegetables can cool – they are meant to be at room temperature or slightly warm.
Assemble: fry eggs in a skillet to your taste.
Place warm rice in bowls.
Top with vegetables and beef, then lastly the egg.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and drizzle with sesame oil. Serve with bibimbap sauce.
Make spice mix: add all ingredients into a small bowl and mix.

Heat oil in a heavy-based non-stick sauté pan over medium-high heat. Once oil is hot, add the finely diced red onion and diced capsicum. Stir-fry for about a minute until the vegetables begin to soften. Then add the ground beef to the pan. Use a spatula to break up the beef as it cooks, ensuring it browns evenly – about 5 minutes.
Once beef is browned, add your spice mix. Stir-fry the mixture for another 3–4 minutes, allowing the spices to fully infuse into the beef.
Assemble dish: place cooked rice in a bowl and spoon over beef mixture. Top with shredded iceberg lettuce, diced tomato and a poached egg. Can also have sour cream and grated cheese.

recipes.title: Ban Fan – Simple Chinese Rice Bowl
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

steps.text: Add the ingredients to a medium heatproof bowl in the order listed – oyster sauce, light soy sauce, sugar, garlic and scallion.
Heat oil in a small saucepan until it starts to smoke.
Drizzle the hot oil over the aromatics and hear it sizzle.
Fry the eggs in the same saucepan. Add warm cooked rice to bowls, top with eggs, and mix well.

recipes.title: Quick Chinese BBQ Pork Mince Bowls

items: 500 g pork mince (or chicken or turkey)

ingredients.heading: To serve
items: Green onion and/or white sesame seeds
Fresh vegetables: cucumber, tomato, grated carrot, steamed broccoli

steps.text: Mix the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat. Cook the onion and garlic for about 1 1/2 minutes until the onion edges turn golden.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink.
Add the sauce and cook on high for 2–3 minutes until it reduces and the pork caramelises.
Serve over rice with vegetables, topped with green onion or sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Salmon Teriyaki with Sautéed Sesame Greens

items: 4 x 180 g salmon fillets, skin on
1 1/4 cups (300 ml) teriyaki sauce (store-bought or see Homemade Teriyaki Sauce)
2 spring onions, sliced on the diagonal, to garnish (optional)

steps.text: Coat the salmon in the teriyaki sauce, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice following the packet directions.

Heat a large frying pan over medium–high heat with half the sesame oil. Fry the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes, then flip gently and cook 2 minutes more, or until cooked through (thicker fillets take longer).
Remove the salmon and cover with foil. Wipe out the pan and reheat over medium heat.
Add the remaining sesame oil and the spinach in batches, stirring until mostly wilted. Stir through the tamari and season.
Serve the salmon on rice with the spinach and avocado, garnished with sesame seeds and spring onion.
If rice is cold, microwave for 1 minute to warm up.
Melt butter in a frypan over medium heat. Add onion and cook until translucent (about 2 minutes).
Add chicken and cook for another couple of minutes. Then add remaining ingredients except rice. Mix well, ensuring that the ingredients are evenly mixed with the tomato ketchup.
Add rice and mix well, ensuring every rice grain is coated in orange colour.
Turn the heat off.
Add eggs, milk, salt and pepper to a bowl and mix well. Try to cut the egg white into small bits by lifting the egg white with a fork occasionally.
Add oil and butter to a non-stick frypan and heat over high heat.
When the butter melts, add the egg mixture and mix well.
While the surface of the egg is still slightly wet but the bottom is cooked, remove the frypan from the heat. Position the frypan with the handle diagonally on your right.
Place the fried rice on the egg, slightly off-centre, allowing 2–3 cm of egg around the rice on the left side of the handle and about 2/3 of the surface of the egg on the other side.

Fold the right side of the egg over the rice. Then shake and tilt the pan to slide the egg with the rice towards the left-hand side of the handle until the edge of the egg reaches the edge of the frypan.
Place a serving plate next to the frypan and gently overturn the frypan to roll the omurice over onto the plate.
Place baking paper over the omurice and use your hands to shape it into a pointy-ended oval shape.
Drizzle tomato ketchup on the top of the omurice.

recipes.title: Egg Foo Young (Chinese Omelette)
recipes.yield: Makes 4 omelettes (2 as a meal, 4 as part of a banquet) | 25 mins

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 1 1/2 Tbsp light or all-purpose soy sauce
1 Tbsp Chinese cooking wine (Shaoxing) or mirin

ingredients.heading: Omelette
items: 4 shallots or green onions, white parts only, sliced

ingredients.heading: Filling (choose one)
items: Prawn: 100–120 g raw small prawns, peeled, deveined and chopped
Pork: 100–120 g pork mince, 1/2 tsp each soy sauce and oyster sauce, pinch of sugar, dash of sesame oil
Garnish (optional): sesame seeds, sliced green onion

steps.text: Sauce: mix the cornflour with the soy sauce until smooth, then stir in the rest. Simmer over medium heat, stirring, for about 1 minute until it thickens to a thin syrup (or microwave 1 1/2 minutes, stir, then 1 1/2 minutes more).
If using pork, mix it with its seasonings.
Whisk the eggs, then mix in the bean sprouts, onion, your filling, salt and pepper (crumble raw pork in by hand).
Heat the oils in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the garlic for 10 seconds and gather it in the centre.
Ladle in a quarter of the mixture and shape into a round. Cook about 1 1/2 minutes until light golden underneath, flip and cook 1 minute more. Repeat.
Pour the sauce over the omelettes, garnish, and serve with rice and steamed vegetables.

items: 4 cups cold cooked rice (day-old is best)
3 green onions, whites and greens separated, sliced
1 Tbsp white pepper (as listed – start with less and add to taste)

steps.text: Mix the egg yolks and a pinch of salt through the cold rice until every grain is coated.
Heat the butter and oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté the garlic and green onion whites for 2–3 minutes.
Push them aside, add the beaten egg whites, let set for about 20 seconds, then scramble.
Add the rice, white pepper and soy sauce and stir-fry on high heat for 2–3 minutes.
Add the green onion tops and stir-fry 1–2 minutes more.

items: 1 1/2 cups cooked short-grain or jasmine rice, hot
Optional additions: kimchi, canned tuna, roasted seaweed flakes, avocado, sautéed vegetables

steps.text: Mix the hot rice with the butter until coated, and put it in a serving bowl. (Reheat cold leftover rice, covered, in the microwave for 2–3 minutes first.)
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and fry the egg sunny side up, spooning hot oil over the white to set it while keeping the yolk runny.
Put the egg on the rice and top with sesame seeds, sesame oil, green onion and soy sauce.
Break the egg and mix everything together. Serve hot.

items: 1-inch knob ginger, cut into thin matchsticks (or 1 Tbsp minced ginger)
4 cups roma tomatoes, roughly chopped (or 2 x 400 g tins chopped tomatoes)
1/3 cup green onions, chopped (reserve some for garnish)

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ginger matchsticks (if using minced ginger, wait until you add the tomato) and cook until fragrant and just starting to brown, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt, white pepper, crushed red chilli flakes, sesame oil and oyster sauce. Toss to combine and continue to cook until the tomatoes are jammy, stirring occasionally, 5 to 8 minutes.

In a small bowl, whisk to combine water and cornstarch for the slurry. Pour the slurry into the pan and stir. Allow the tomatoes to continue cooking until broken down and thickened, 2–3 minutes. Reduce heat to maintain a simmer.

Drizzle the eggs over the tomatoes and do not stir. Let the eggs gently cook in the tomatoes until just barely set, 2 minutes. Add the green onions and then gently stir to break up the egg. Don't stir too much.
Serve the tomato egg with steamed rice and garnish with chopped green onions.

ingredients.heading: Meatballs
items: Pinch of white pepper and salt
2 tsp lemongrass paste (or fresh, finely chopped)

steps.text: Sauce: mix ingredients. Set aside for 10 minutes.
Noodles: pour over boiling water and soak per packet directions. Drain and set aside.
Meatballs: mix all ingredients except oil until combined.
Shape into 6 mini hamburger patties with your hands.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add patties and cook for 2 1/2 minutes or until golden. Flip, cook 2 minutes, then remove.
Assemble bowls: place noodles in bowl. Top with a handful of beansprouts, and wedge in lettuce, carrots and radish.
Place meatballs on top.
Spoon over sauce (like a soup broth, to taste).

recipes.title: Chinese Dumplings
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life
introNotes: Adjust recipe to size as required (this recipe makes about 84–96 dumplings).

items: 1.35 kg green leafy vegetables (e.g. baby bok choy, napa cabbage)

steps.text: Wash your vegetables thoroughly and blanch them in a pot of boiling water. Transfer them to an ice bath to cool. Wring out all the water from the vegetables and chop very finely.
In a large bowl, stir together the vegetables, meat, wine, oil, sesame oil, salt, soy sauce, white pepper and 2/3 cup water. Mix for 6–8 minutes, until very well combined.

To wrap dumplings, dampen the edges of each circle with some water. Put filling in the middle. Fold the wrapper in half and pinch together at the top. Then make two folds on each side, until the dumpling looks like a fan. Make sure it's completely sealed. Repeat until all the filling is gone, placing the dumplings on a baking sheet lined with parchment. Make sure the dumplings aren't sticking together.

If you'd like to freeze them, wrap the baking sheets tightly with plastic wrap and put the pans in the freezer. Allow to freeze overnight, then transfer dumplings to ziplock bags and put back into the freezer.
To cook dumplings, boil or pan-fry them.
Boil: simply bring a large pot of water to a boil, drop the dumplings in, and cook until they float to the top and the skins are cooked through but still slightly al dente.

Pan-fry: heat 2 Tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place the dumplings in the pan and allow to fry for 2 minutes. Pour a thin layer of water into the pan, cover, and reduce heat to medium-low. Allow dumplings to steam until the water has evaporated. Remove the cover, increase heat to medium-high and allow to fry for a few more minutes, until the bottoms of the dumplings are golden brown and crisp.
Serve with soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, chilli sauce, or any other dipping sauce of your choice.

recipes.title: Simple Wonton Soup
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life
introNotes: Recipe has been doubled. Adjust soup quantity as required.

items: 600 g baby bok choy or wombok
5 Tbsp sesame oil, plus more for the stock
12 cups chicken stock (adjust to quantity of soup required to serve)

steps.text: Start by thoroughly washing the vegetables. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the vegetables just until wilted, about 60–90 seconds. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Carefully squeeze out as much water as you can from the vegetables. Very finely chop the vegetables.

In a medium bowl, add the finely chopped vegetables, pork mince, 5 Tbsp sesame oil, pinch of white pepper, 2 Tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp salt and 4 Tbsp Shaoxing wine. Mix very thoroughly until the mixture is totally emulsified – almost like a paste.

To assemble wontons, fill a small bowl with water. Grab a wrapper and use your fingers to moisten the edges of the wrapper. Add a little over a teaspoon of filling in the middle. Fold the wrapper in half and press the two sides together so you get a firm seal.
Hold the bottom two corners of the little rectangle you just made (the side where the filling is) and bring the two corners together. You can use a little bit of water to make sure they stick.
Place the wontons on a baking sheet, and make sure they are not touching. To freeze: cover tray of wontons with plastic wrap, place in freezer, then transfer them to freezer bags once they're frozen.
To make soup, heat your chicken stock to a simmer and add teaspoons of sesame oil, and white pepper and salt to taste.

Bring a separate pot of water to a boil. Carefully add the wontons one at a time to the pot. Pick up the pot and use a swirling, twisting motion to keep the water moving and prevent the wontons from sticking to the bottom (if they stick, don't worry, they should come free once cooked). Once they're floating, boil them for another 1–2 minutes. Take care not to overcook them. Remove wontons with a slotted spoon and put them in bowls.
Pour the soup over the wontons and garnish with scallions. Serve.

recipes.title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

steps.text: Cut the pork into long strips or chunks about 5–8 cm thick. Don't trim any excess fat, as it will render off and add flavour.
Combine the sugar, salt, five spice powder, white pepper, sesame oil, wine, soy sauce, hoisin sauce, molasses/golden syrup, food colouring (if using) and garlic in a bowl to make the marinade.

Reserve about 2 Tbsp of marinade and set it aside. Rub the pork with the rest of the marinade in a large bowl or baking dish. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours. Cover and store the reserved marinade in the fridge as well.
Preheat your oven to bake at 246 °C with a rack positioned in the upper third of the oven. It is recommended to check your char siu every 10 minutes, reducing or increasing temperature as needed.

Line a sheet pan with foil and place a metal rack on top. Place the pork on the rack, leaving as much space as possible between pieces. Pour 1 1/2 cups water into the pan below the rack (this prevents any drippings from burning or smoking).

Transfer the pork to your preheated oven. Roast for 25 minutes, keeping the oven at 246 °C for the first 10 minutes of roasting, and then reduce temperature to 190 °C. After 25 minutes, flip the pork. Add more water to the bottom of the pan if dry. Turn the pan 180° to ensure even roasting. Roast another 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine the reserved marinade with the honey and 1 Tbsp hot water. This will be the sauce you'll use for basting the pork.
After 40 minutes of total roasting time, baste the pork, flip it, and baste the other side as well. Roast for a final 10 minutes.
Remove from oven and baste the last bit. Let the meat rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Crispy Pork Belly (Chinese Siu Yuk)
recipes.source: Recipe from kwokspots.com (method summarised; temperatures converted from °F)
recipes.time: Prep 10 mins, cook 2 hrs, rest 12 hrs (overnight) – total about 14 hrs 10 mins

ingredients.heading: Pork belly
items: 1.8 kg (4 lb) skin-on pork belly (makes 2 portions)
1/2 cup kosher salt (or other coarse salt), for topping

steps.text: Cut the pork belly in half so each piece is a slab of about 20 x 15 cm (8 x 6 inches).
Cut vertical slits about 1 cm (1/2 inch) deep into the meat side. Season only the meat side with the five spice, brown sugar, garlic powder and salt.
Place skin side up on a wire rack in the fridge overnight, uncovered, so the skin dries out.
The next day, wrap a snug foil "boat" around the meat side and edges of each piece, leaving the skin exposed. This stops the meat from burning.
Brush the skin with the oil or vinegar, then cover the skin completely with the coarse salt. Use kosher or another coarse salt so it doesn't soak into the skin – fine sea salt is too fine.
Bake in the oven at 150 °C (300 °F) for 1 1/2 hours. The meat will shrink and the pork will sit taller. Use the oven, not the air fryer, for this step, as the air fryer fan will blow the salt away.
Remove all the salt from the skin and brush the skin with a layer of oil.
Air fry at 230 °C (450 °F) for about 20 minutes, until the skin is puffed, light and crispy. No air fryer: use the oven on its highest fan-forced setting.
Cut into pieces and serve with the hoisin sauce mixed 1:1 with water.

recipes.title: Char Siu Bao (Steamed BBQ Pork Buns)
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

ingredients.heading: Steamed char siu bao dough (double-recipe amounts in brackets)
items: 1 tsp active dry yeast (3 g) [double: 2 tsp]

ingredients.heading: Steamed bao filling (double-recipe amounts in brackets)
items: 1/3 cup shallots/red onion, finely chopped [double: 2/3 cup]
1 1/2 cups diced Chinese roast pork (Char Siu – see recipe) [double: 3 cups]

steps.text: In the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Sift together the flour and cornstarch and add it to the yeast mixture along with the sugar and oil. Turn on the mixer to the lowest setting and let it go until a smooth dough ball is formed. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for 2 hours.

While the dough is resting, make the meat filling. Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the onion and stir-fry for a minute. Turn heat down to medium-low and add the sugar, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil and dark soy. Stir and cook until the mixture starts to bubble up. Add the chicken stock and flour, cooking for a couple of minutes until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the roast pork. Set aside to cool. If you make the filling ahead of time, cover and refrigerate to prevent it from drying out.

After your dough has rested for 2 hours, add the baking powder to the dough and turn the mixer on to the lowest setting. At this point, if the dough looks dry or you're having trouble incorporating the baking powder, add 1–2 tsp water. Gently knead the dough until it becomes smooth again. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for another 15 minutes. In the meantime, get a large piece of parchment paper and cut it into ten 4 x 4 inch squares. Prepare your steamer by bringing the water to a boil.

Now we are ready to assemble the buns: roll the dough into a long tube and divide it into 10 equal pieces. Press each piece of dough into a disc about 4 1/2 inches in diameter (it should be thicker in the centre and thinner around the edges). Add some filling and pleat the buns until they're closed on top.

Place each bun on a parchment paper square and steam. Be sure the boiling water does not touch the buns during the steaming process. Once the water boils, place the buns in the steamer and steam each batch for 12 minutes over high heat.

notes: The sauce is strong when doubled – some ingredients should be reduced.

ingredients.heading: Optional
items: 1 large onion, quartered and thinly sliced
3 cups (90 g) butter lettuce leaves, roughly torn

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 260 °C.
Quick carrot pickle: stir 1 Tbsp sugar into 3 Tbsp rice vinegar until dissolved, then toss with the carrot and set aside (or skip and use raw carrot).

Sauce: warm the gochujang, honey, garlic, remaining 1 Tbsp sugar, remaining 3 Tbsp vinegar, sesame oil and soy sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat until almost simmering. Thin with water if needed.
Score the pork skin at 1 cm intervals without cutting into the meat. Rub in the salt and roast for 20 minutes, then reduce to 160 °C and roast 10 minutes more. Rest for 10 minutes.
Cut the pork into 1 cm slices and coat with half the sauce. Fry in a large pan over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until cooked through and sticky.
Steam the buns for 10 minutes.
Fill the buns with pork, spoon over the remaining sauce and add pickled carrot, cucumber, lettuce and onion as you like.

items: 200 g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting

steps.text: Make the dough in a large bowl. Combine the self-raising flour and the Greek yoghurt. Stir using chopsticks or a wooden spoon. Knead for 5 minutes until you have a bouncy, soft dough. Cover with cling film and set aside for 10 minutes.

Get your dough and pierce it in the middle with your finger. Form a donut and then slice the donut to make a log. Slice your dough log into 10 equal pieces. Roll each piece out into a circular wrapper that is around 1/2 cm thick and 3 inches in diameter. Sprinkle with flour to keep them from sticking.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre and seal.
Place dumplings onto little pieces of baking paper and place into steamer. Steam for 10–15 minutes, then remove.
Optional: heat pan over medium heat and drizzle with oil. Add your dumplings face up and fry for 4 minutes until underside is golden and crispy. Remove from pan and serve warm.

items: 1 small yellow capsicum, seeded and finely chopped
1 small red capsicum, seeded and finely chopped

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and carrot and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes or until onion softens. Add the mince and garlic and cook, stirring with a wooden spoon to break up lumps, for 5 minutes or until the mince changes colour. Add the zucchini, combined capsicum and eggplant and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes or until the vegetables are just tender.

Add tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1 minute or until well combined. Add the tomato, pasta sauce, stock and oregano and bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
Meanwhile, cook pasta in a saucepan of boiling water following packet directions or until al dente. Drain well.
Divide the pasta among serving bowls. Spoon over the mince mixture and season with pepper to serve.

items: 1/2 tsp salt, plus more as needed
1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, plus more as needed

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large, high-sided sauté pan over medium heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and sauté until softened and translucent, 3–4 minutes.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, if using, and sauté until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Carefully pour in the tomatoes. Add the salt and pepper and stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer and cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and stir in the cream. Taste and season with additional salt and pepper as needed.
Meanwhile, cook pasta as per package instructions.
Drain the pasta and add it to the sauce. Toss gently to combine.

recipes.title: Homemade Tomato Pasta Sauce (with Topping) (Vegetarian)
recipes.source: Recipe adapted from The Spruce Eats

items: Topping: zucchini (chopped), red onion and garlic salt

steps.text: Topping: chop zucchini and red onion, sprinkle with garlic salt and let sit for at least 10 minutes, then caramelise in a pan.
Blanch the tomatoes: plunge tomatoes into boiling water for 1–2 minutes to loosen skins. Rinse tomatoes in cool water, set aside to cool and drain.
Remove the skins, stems and seeds, then slice the tomatoes into quarters/halves.
Add 1/4 cup olive oil to a large pot. Sauté the onions until soft, add garlic and stir for 30 seconds. (Can add carrots or peppers/capsicum with the onion.)

Add the tomatoes and spices, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar to the onion-garlic mixture. Bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring frequently, for about 2–3 hours until desired thickness is achieved.
Serve mixed with pasta, topped with cheese and zucchini topping.

recipes.title: Fettuccine with Cherry Tomato Butter Sauce

steps.text: In a large pan, sauté the onion in butter over medium-low heat until soft (about 5 minutes), then add the tomatoes. Season with a teaspoon of salt.

Cook the sauce over medium for 30–35 minutes (stir frequently and lower heat if scorching) or until the cherry tomatoes have burst and softened and the butter has completely blended in with the tomatoes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. When the sauce is almost ready, begin boiling the fettuccine to 1 minute less than al dente.
A few minutes before the pasta finishes cooking, add 1 cup pasta water to the sauce and stir to combine. Continue to cook the sauce over medium heat.
Add the pasta to the sauce and toss to coat. Cook until pasta is done, turn off heat and season to taste. Add herbs, toss and serve.

items: 3/4 cup (185 ml) cooking cream (light thickened cream)

steps.text: Cook pasta in a large saucepan of boiling water until just tender, following packet instructions. Drain and return to pan over low heat.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a medium frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook garlic and bacon, stirring, for 3–4 minutes or until crisp. Set aside.

Whisk eggs, cream and 3/4 cup of the parmesan in a large jug. Season with pepper. Add egg mixture, half the parsley and half the bacon mixture to pasta. Toss gently to combine and warm through (do not overheat).
Serve pasta topped with remaining parsley, bacon and parmesan.

recipes.title: Pasta with Leek and Bacon (and Zucchini)

items: 3/4 cup white wine (or equivalent, i.e. chicken stock/part white wine vinegar)

steps.text: Wash and slice leeks. Chop bacon into pieces.
Fry butter in pan and add bacon, leeks, mushrooms and zucchini.
When mixture softens, add the crushed garlic.
Add the white wine and allow to bubble, then lower heat and add cream.
Stir through and simmer.
Add a little cornflour to thicken.
Add cheese and stir through, and continue to simmer for a few minutes.
Add fresh parsley if desired. Stir pasta through sauce.
Serve.

items: 450 g spaghetti (pasta), cooked and drained, 1/4 cup pasta water reserved
2 large leeks, trimmed, sliced and cleaned

steps.text: Cook pasta (slightly undercook), setting aside 1/4 cup pasta water. Drain pasta and set aside.
In a large pan over medium heat, add the butter, onions, leeks, salt and ground black pepper. Stir together, and cook until onions are translucent and the leeks have wilted a bit – about 5 minutes.
Next, add the garlic and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add the milk and parmesan cheese. Stir to combine.
Add the cooked pasta and toss with tongs until well coated.
If the butter and milk sauce is too thick, add some of the reserved pasta water.
Cook, continuing to toss, for 2 minutes to reheat pasta.
Plate and garnish with parmesan and parsley.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add the fettuccine and cook according to package directions, minus 1 minute. Reserve about 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain pasta.
While pasta is cooking, melt butter in a large, heavy-based pan over medium-low heat. As soon as butter is melted, turn heat off.
Add pasta to pan with butter and toss gently. Gradually add the parmesan, gently tossing until cheese is melted and forms a creamy sauce.
Add reserved pasta water, 1–2 Tbsp at a time, tossing gently until desired consistency is reached. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook pasta according to package directions (or slightly less). Drain.
Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter and olive oil.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the cream, thyme, oregano, salt and pepper and bring the sauce to a high simmer (the sauce should be steaming with small bubbles forming on the edges but not quite boiling).
Reduce the heat to medium-low, and cook, stirring often, until the sauce is thickened slightly, about 5 minutes.

Slowly stir in the cheese and parmesan, and continue cooking until cheese is melted and the sauce is thick and smooth. The sauce will continue to thicken as it cools on the pasta (can add a splash of pasta water).
Keep sauce warm until pasta is ready.
Cook pasta. Drain.
Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Whisk in the flour, and cook, stirring constantly, until it's lightly browned, about 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk, stirring until it is incorporated and smooth.
Add the thyme, oregano, salt, pepper and parmesan and whisk continuously for 3–4 minutes until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Reduce the heat to a low simmer until the pasta is ready.

items: 1/2 cup dry white wine (or extra chicken stock)

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 1 1/2 minutes less than the packet time. Save a mugful of pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, season the chicken. Melt half the butter in a large skillet over high heat and cook the chicken about 2 minutes each side until deep golden. Rest briefly, then shred with two forks.
Turn the heat to medium–high, add the remaining butter and the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add the wine and simmer, scraping up the browned bits, until mostly evaporated.
Add the stock, cream, parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes and simmer, stirring, for 3–5 minutes (it will still look thin).
Add the spinach, chicken and pasta and toss for 1 1/2–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the pasta. Loosen with pasta water if needed.
Serve straight away with parmesan, bacon and parsley.
Use a pan wide enough to lay the pasta flat and deep enough to stir without spilling.
Season the chicken. Heat the oil over medium–high heat and cook the chicken 2 minutes each side until golden and cooked. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Add the milk, stock and garlic to the pan and bring to a simmer. Add the pasta and move it around every 30 seconds for about 3 minutes until it softens, then reduce to medium and stir every couple of minutes.
After 9–10 minutes, when the pasta is nearly cooked and a little liquid still covers the base, stir in the cream and parmesan.
Simmer about 2 minutes until thick and the pasta is cooked; add a splash of hot water if it gets gluey. Season.
Serve with the chicken, parsley and extra parmesan.

recipes.title: One Pot Creamy Tomato Beef Pasta

items: To serve: finely grated parmesan, chopped parsley (optional)

steps.text: Heat the oil on high in a large heavy-based pot. Cook the garlic and onion for 1 1/2 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the herbs for 30 seconds, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, salt, pepper and chilli, stir, then add the pasta.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is just about cooked.
Add the cream and simmer 1–2 minutes – it should still be quite saucy.
Serve with parmesan and parsley.

recipes.title: One-Pot Creamy Beef Pasta (Cheddar & Parmesan)
recipes.source: Butter Be Ready (butterbeready.com) – method summarised; converted to metric

items: Salt and black pepper, to taste
450 g (1 lb) dried short pasta (rigatoni suggested)
4 cups (1 L) chicken or beef stock
225 g (8 oz) shredded sharp white cheddar
1 cup freshly grated parmesan, plus extra for topping

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium–high heat. Brown the beef, breaking it up, for 6–7 minutes, then season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Stir in the shallot and cook 4–5 minutes more.
Add the pasta and stock, stir, cover and simmer for 10–12 minutes until the pasta is al dente.
Turn off the heat and stir in the cream and both cheeses. Cover and leave for at least 10 minutes to thicken, then serve with extra parmesan.

recipes.title: One Pot Cajun Beef Pasta (Lots of Veg)

ingredients.heading: One-pot pasta
