items: 350 g (3 cups) uncooked short pasta (macaroni, spirals, penne, shells, rigatoni)
1 1/2 cups tightly packed Colby or other melting cheese

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot (with a lid) over high heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the beef and brown it, breaking it up.
Add the carrot and zucchini and cook 2 minutes until most of their water has evaporated, then the capsicum for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and Cajun spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, water, stock and beans, mix well and bring to a simmer. Stir in the pasta, return to a simmer, then cover and lower to medium for a gentle simmer.
Cook 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it doesn't catch – the pasta should be slightly firm and still soupy.
Stir, smooth the top and scatter over the cheese. Cover, turn off the heat and leave 3 minutes to melt the cheese and finish the pasta.
Sprinkle with green onion and serve.

items: 560 g Coles Herb & Garlic Beef Sausages, casings removed
2 x 280 g jars Coles Chargrilled Vegetables, drained, reserving 1/3 cup (80 ml) oil

steps.text: Cook the pasta until al dente; drain, keeping 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the cooking water.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the sausage meat for about 5 minutes, breaking up lumps with a wooden spoon, until golden.
Stir in the chargrilled vegetables, the reserved oil, the pasta, the reserved cooking water and 3/4 cup (65 g) of the parmesan. Toss together.
Serve in bowls topped with the remaining parmesan and the basil. Season.

items: 2 x 95 g cans Sirena Tuna Chunky Tomato & Basil

steps.text: Cook the pasta until al dente; drain, keeping 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the tomatoes for about 4 minutes, turning, until they start to collapse. Set aside on a plate and keep warm.
Cook the zucchini, mushroom and garlic in the pan for about 4 minutes, until softened. Season.
Add the pasta, reserved water, cream, chilli (if using) and tuna with its sauce. Toss for about 1 minute until hot.
Serve topped with the tomatoes and a sprinkle of parmesan.

items: 500 g Coles Deli Aussie Raw Peeled Prawns
120 g packet Coles Australian Baby Spinach

steps.text: Cook the pasta until al dente and drain.
Heat a large frying pan over high heat and spray with olive oil. Cook the prawns for 3–4 minutes, turning, until they curl and change colour.
Stir in the pasta sauce for 2–3 minutes until hot. Add the spinach and chilli (if using) and toss.
Add the pasta to the pan and toss until combined and heated through. Season.

recipes.title: Honey Mustard and Bacon Pasta Bake

items: 500 g penne (or other short pasta, e.g. spirals or shells)
1 cup (120 g) coarsely grated tasty cheddar

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200 °C. Cook pasta in a saucepan of boiling water following packet directions until al dente. Drain.
Meanwhile, heat a medium frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the bacon and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes or until crisp. Whisk the cream, mustard and honey in a medium bowl. Season.

Transfer the pasta to a 12-cup (3 L) ovenproof dish. Add the bacon and spring onion and stir to combine. Add the cream mixture and stir to combine. Sprinkle evenly with cheddar. Bake for 20–25 minutes or until golden brown.
Sprinkle with parsley to serve.

recipes.title: Cheesy Rarebit Pasta Bake

items: 1/3 cup (80 ml) stout beer (or vegetable stock)

steps.text: Cook the pasta in boiling water for 3 minutes (it will still be firm). Drain and spread on a tray to cool.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium–low heat, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the cream, beer and 1/2 cup (125 ml) water. Bring to the boil and stir for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the Worcestershire and mustard, take off the heat and whisk in the cheddar. Season and stir through the pasta. Spoon into a 1.1 L ovenproof dish.
Crispy crumbs: melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the panko for 2 minutes until golden. Stir in the parsley and salt.
Sprinkle the crumbs over the pasta and serve with salad leaves.

notes: To freeze, cool completely and freeze (without the crumbs) for up to 1 month. Thaw overnight, then bake covered at 160 °C for 50–60 minutes, stirring halfway, before adding the crumbs.

items: 500 g chicken breast, trimmed and thinly sliced
1 red capsicum, seeded and thinly sliced
1 Tbsp Australian mustard, or grain mustard
100 g snow peas, trimmed and sliced
2 Tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a frying pan on high. Brown chicken for 3–4 minutes until cooked through. Transfer to a plate.

Heat remaining oil in the same pan on high. Sauté capsicum, onion and garlic for 5 minutes until tender. Stir in honey and mustard, then the cream. Simmer, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return chicken to pan with snow peas and parsley. Heat gently for 2–3 minutes. Serve on risoni, sprinkled with extra parsley.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan-forced).
Heat the oil in an ovenproof pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook for 1–2 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

Add onion and garlic and cook 2–3 minutes or until the onion has softened. Stir in passata and stock, reduce heat and bring to a simmer. Add oregano, stir through the risoni, then place the cooked chicken thighs over the top. Cover with a lid or foil and bake in the oven for 10 minutes.
Remove lid and sprinkle mozzarella over the chicken. Return to the oven with the lid off and bake a further 10 minutes, or until cheese has melted and is golden. Serve immediately.

ingredients.heading: Meatballs (makes about 16)
items: 50 g mozzarella, cut into 16 cubes (about 1 cm)

ingredients.heading: Sauce
items: 100 g freshly grated parmesan, plus extra to serve
7 g basil leaves, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Mix the meatball ingredients (except the mozzarella) until just combined. Roll into balls of about 2 heaped tablespoons.
Flatten each ball, press a mozzarella cube into the centre and re-roll to seal it in.
Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium–high heat and brown the meatballs all over for 4–6 minutes. Set aside.
Drain excess oil (add 1 Tbsp water to lift sticky bits if needed). Cook the onion and garlic for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the risoni, stock, passata, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, stirring regularly.
Stir in the parmesan and basil, return the meatballs, cover and cook 3–5 minutes until the cheese melts and the meatballs are hot.
Serve with extra parmesan and basil.

items: 1/2 large red onion, cut into 1/2-inch-thick wedges
4 Tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
1 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more
1 cup basil leaves (or a few shakes of dried)

steps.text: Place a rack in the middle of the oven; preheat to 220 °C. Toss onion, garlic, tomatoes, gnocchi, 3 Tbsp oil and 3/4 tsp salt on a rimmed baking sheet to coat; season generously with pepper and toss again to combine.
Roast, stirring once or twice, until gnocchi are golden and starting to crisp, most of the tomatoes have burst, and onion is golden, 25–30 minutes.
Remove garlic from baking sheet, peel, and place in a small bowl. Mash with 1/4 tsp salt. Whisk in lemon juice and remaining 1 Tbsp oil; season dressing with pepper and more salt if needed.
Add rocket, basil and parmesan to baking sheet and drizzle dressing over; toss to combine. Divide among plates and drizzle with a little more oil.

items: 6 cups (1.5 L) chicken or vegetable stock
1 large leek, pale section only, thinly sliced
2 bunches asparagus, woody ends trimmed, cut into 5 cm lengths

steps.text: Bring stock to the boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to low and keep at a gentle simmer.
Heat a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the pancetta for 1 minute each side or until crisp. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel.

Add half the butter, half the oil and the leek to the large saucepan. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes or until leek softens. Transfer to a bowl. Add remaining butter, remaining oil, onion and garlic to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes or until the onion softens. Add the rice. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute or until grains appear glassy. Add wine. Bring to the boil. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes or until absorbed. Add 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the stock and cook, stirring, until the liquid is completely absorbed. Repeat with remaining stock, stirring constantly and allowing the liquid to be absorbed before adding more, until rice is tender yet firm to the bite and the risotto is creamy (this should take about 20 minutes).

Add the asparagus. Cook for 1 minute or until bright green and tender. Coarsely tear the pancetta into pieces. Add to the pan with the leek, lemon zest and lemon juice. Stir to combine. Remove from heat. Stir in parmesan. Divide among serving bowls.

items: 450 g pkt Beef & Pork Chorizo Sausages

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage and cook, turning, for 8 minutes or until cooked through and brown all over. Thickly slice.

Heat the remaining oil in the pan. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes or until onion softens. Add the capsicum, zucchini and paprika. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes or until aromatic. Add the rice and stock and stir to combine. Season. Bring to the boil, then reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes or until the rice is (just) tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Top the rice mixture with peas and sausage. Cover, and cook for 5 minutes or until heated through. Drizzle with lemon juice as desired.

recipes.title: Cheat's Sausage Risotto with Roasted Broccoli

items: 550 g garlic and herb beef sausages, torn into bite-sized pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Dissolve the stock cubes in 4 1/2 cups (1.125 L) water in a medium saucepan, bring to the boil, then keep at a low simmer.
Heat a large saucepan over high heat and cook the sausage in two batches for 5 minutes, stirring, until browned and cooked. Set aside, covered.

Add the rice to the pan and stir for 1 minute to soak up the sausage oil. Add 1/2 cup stock and stir 2 minutes until absorbed. Pour in the rest of the stock, stir, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Meanwhile, roast the broccoli on a tray for 10 minutes until tender and charred.
Fold the sausage, broccoli and half the parmesan through the risotto. Serve sprinkled with the remaining parmesan.
Peel and chop onions, garlic, carrots, celery and peppers finely.
Heat a large pan on medium-high heat. Add 2 Tbsp oil and sauté the vegetables.
Add chilli powder, cumin and cinnamon with a pinch of salt and pepper. Stir and cook for about 7 minutes.
Add drained and rinsed chickpeas and kidney beans, and the tomatoes.
Add minced beef, breaking up chunks with a wooden spoon.
Fill one of the empty tins with water and add to pan.
Add the balsamic vinegar.
Bring to the boil and turn heat down to simmer with lid slightly askew for 1 hour, stirring every now and again.
Serve with rice and top with cheese, sour cream, fried shallots etc.

items: 1 whole onion, diced (I add diced capsicum/mushrooms)
Toppings: grated cheese, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, diced avocado, sour cream

steps.text: In a frypan, heat oil and cook onion, capsicum and mushrooms. Add minced beef and cook until totally browned.
Add spices and salt and pepper.
Add the beans and hot water. Stir.
Reduce heat and simmer.
Serve over corn chips with toppings.
Grate the onion into a large bowl using a box grater. Add panko and mix briefly to coat in the onion juices.

Grate zucchini and carrot into the bowl. Add remaining ingredients. Mix well. Scoop up about 1/4 cup of mixture and form a 1.7 cm thick pattie. Indent the middle slightly. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add half the patties and cook for 4 minutes or until dark golden. Press lightly with a spatula (if you press hard the juices will come out).
Flip and cook the other side for 3–4 minutes until golden.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining rissoles. Serve with tomato ketchup.

recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs in Cream Sauce

items: Pickled lingonberries or lingonberry jam, to serve

ingredients.heading: Meatballs
items: 1 1/2 cups (110 g) loosely packed fresh breadcrumbs

ingredients.heading: Mashed potatoes
items: 1 Tbsp salt, plus extra for seasoning
200 g butter, chilled and cut into cubes

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C.

Mash: cover the potatoes with cold water, add the salt and bring to the boil. Cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain, return to the dry pan over very low heat for 1 minute, then turn off the heat and let steam off for 5 minutes. Mash well, add the butter, then gradually stir in the milk. Season with sea salt.

Meatballs: soak the breadcrumbs in the cream for a few minutes, then mix in the pork, beef, onion, nutmeg, salt and white pepper. Roll into small balls and place on a large baking tray. Pour a little water into the tray and bake for 10–15 minutes, until just cooked through. Drain.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat until very hot. Add half the butter and brown the meatballs well all over, about 5 minutes (in batches if needed). Remove and keep warm – don't wash the pan.

Sauce: add the remaining butter to the pan over medium heat, sprinkle in the flour and stir, scraping up the browned bits. Add the stock a little at a time, bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the cream. Season to taste.
Serve the meatballs drizzled with the sauce, with the mash, pickled cucumbers and lingonberries.

notes: The key to a good Swedish meatball is the well-browned surface from frying, not the sauce.

items: 5 large potatoes (Yukon Gold or equivalent), peeled and cut into 1/4 inch (about 6 mm) cubes
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Gather all ingredients.
Melt butter with olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion until lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in potatoes and carrot; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in corned beef, parsley, pepper, thyme and salt. Cook, stirring often, until hash is crisp and browned, 10 to 15 more minutes.
Serve with fried egg (optional).

recipes.title: Curried Sausages (Aunty Leanne's Recipe)

steps.text: Boil sausages in a saucepan of water and remove skins.
Cut into bite-size pieces (6 per sausage).
Heat an electric frypan with 1 Tbsp oil and add onion and sausages.
Fry until onion is slightly cooked.
Mix remaining ingredients in a bowl and pour over sausage mix in frypan.
Cook on low, stirring occasionally, until cooked (about 10–20 minutes).

notes: Serve with rice or mashed potato and veges.

items: 1 apple or pear, cored and sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the sausages for 4–5 minutes over a low to medium heat until browned. Add the onions and apple/pear, then cook for a further 2 minutes. Drain off any excess oil.
Combine the tomato sauce, cornflour, Worcestershire sauce, spices and brown sugar with 2 cups of water, then whisk to mix well.
Pour the sauce mix into the pan and mix well. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sausages are cooked and the sauce thickens.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

items: 500 g pork scotch fillet steaks, patted dry

steps.text: Mix the water, honey, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl. Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Heat a large non-stick pan over high heat with 2 Tbsp butter. Sear the pork 1 minute each side, then lower to medium and cook 4–5 minutes each side. Rest 5 minutes.
In the same pan, melt another 2 Tbsp butter and cook the garlic until fragrant. Return the pork with the sauce and boil for 1 minute until thick and sticky.
Take off the heat and stir in the last 1 Tbsp butter. Serve with hot rice, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

ingredients.heading: Burrito seasoning
items: 1 tsp each onion powder, dried oregano and salt
2 tsp each ground cumin and paprika
3/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, adjust to taste)

ingredients.heading: Rice (choose one)
items: 2 1/2 cups cooked plain white rice, or Mexican red rice

ingredients.heading: Other fillings
items: 400 g can corn, drained (or 280 g frozen, thawed)
To serve: avocado sauce, sour cream or smooth salsa

steps.text: Mix the seasoning. Coat the chicken with 1 Tbsp oil, then sprinkle with the seasoning.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the chicken 2 minutes, turn and cook 1 1/2 minutes more. Rest 2 minutes, then chop.
In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic for 1 minute, then the capsicum for 2 minutes.
Add the refried beans, chicken and water and cook 2 minutes until slightly reduced. Cool 5 minutes to thicken.
Warm the tortillas. Put rice on the lower third, then filling, corn, cheese and coriander. Fold up burrito-style.
Toast in a dry pan over medium–high heat for 2 minutes each side, or wrap in foil and bake at 180 °C for 10 minutes.
Serve with your choice of sauce.

recipes.title: Freezer Beef & Bean Burritos
recipes.source: Easy Weeknight Recipes (easyweeknightrecipes.com) – method summarised; converted to metric
recipes.yield: Makes 10 burritos | Prep 10 mins | Cook 20 mins

items: 1/4 cup grated or finely diced brown onion
2 Tbsp taco seasoning (or a 30 g packet)
2 x 400 g cans pinto beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 20 seconds.
Add the beef and cook about 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and salsa and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Take off the heat.
Blend the beans with the stock until smooth (about 1 minute), stir into the beef, then mix in the cheese.
Put 2 Tbsp rice (if using) in the centre of each tortilla, top with 1/2 cup filling, fold in the ends and sides and roll up.
To freeze: wrap each burrito in baking/wax paper and then foil. Pack into a large freezer bag, press out the air, label and freeze for up to 2 months.

To reheat from frozen: remove the foil, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 2–3 minutes, turning halfway; rest 1 minute. Or bake still in foil at 180 °C for 30–40 minutes until hot in the centre.
From the fridge: thaw overnight, then microwave 1–2 minutes, turning halfway.
Heat oil in a medium pan, then fry onions until golden. Add the beef mince and garlic and fry on medium heat until meat is browned.
Add the remaining beef mix ingredients and cook covered on low heat for around 20 minutes.
When the beef mixture is almost ready, beat the eggs and cream cheese in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan on medium to low heat, then add the egg mixture. Cook the eggs slowly, mixing constantly, until golden and still a bit runny. Take out of the pan.
To assemble: soften the tortilla in a pan or microwave. Lay tortilla flat and layer cheese, meat, scrambled egg mixture, tomatoes and spring onions.
Wrap the tortilla and place on a medium-hot pan to seal the edges and toast all sides.

items: 800 g sirloin steak, cut into 1.5 cm chunks

steps.text: Mix the ginger, garlic, gochujang, sesame oil, brown sugar and tamari. Toss with the beef in a large sealable container, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Tip the beef and all the marinade into a slow cooker and cook on low for 6 hours until tender. Season.
Warm the tortillas following the packet directions, fill with beef and top with rocket and your favourite taco toppings.

recipes.title: Smoky Bourbon & Maple Pulled Pork Burgers (Pressure Cooker or Slow Cooker)
recipes.source: Cookbook – "From the pressure cooker" / "From the slow cooker" (method summarised)
recipes.yield: Makes 8 | Pressure cooker 2 1/4 hrs; slow cooker 9 hrs

items: 1 Tbsp olive oil (slow cooker version: 2 Tbsp)
1.8 kg boneless pork shoulder, trimmed, tied
1/2 tsp ground allspice (slow cooker version: 2 tsp)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a 6-litre pressure cooker and brown the pork all over, about 10 minutes. Remove. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add three-quarters of the garlic and the spices and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return the pork with the passata, stock, bourbon, mustard, chipotle, maple syrup, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves. Season. Lock the lid, bring to low pressure, then reduce the heat to keep it steady and cook for 1 1/4 hours.

Quick-release the pressure and remove the lid. Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then shred. Boil the cooking liquid over medium heat for 10 minutes until thickened, return the pork, toss in the sauce and season.

Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium–high heat and brown the pork for 10 minutes; remove. Whisk the stock, passata, bourbon, mustard, chipotle, vinegar, maple syrup, thyme and bay leaves in a jug.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add three-quarters of the garlic and the spices and cook 1 minute. Add the passata mixture, scraping up the browned bits.
Transfer the pork and sauce to a 5.5-litre slow cooker, season, and cook covered on low for 8 hours (or high for 5 hours).
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then shred. Strain the cooking liquid into a large frying pan and boil over medium–high heat for 8 minutes until thickened. Add the pork, toss to coat and season.
Preheat the grill to high. Split the buns and toast, cut side up, until golden.
Slaw: whisk the buttermilk, sour cream, mayonnaise, lime juice and remaining garlic in a large bowl, then toss through the coleslaw mix.
Fill the buns with slaw and pulled pork. Serve with oven fries if you like.

notes: The pork freezes well once cooked (before shredding and saucing). With an electric pressure cooker you don't need to adjust the heat to stabilise the pressure – follow the manufacturer's instructions.

items: 1.5 kg boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 cups chicken broth (1 tsp stock powder + 2 cups water)

steps.text: In a large skillet, cook bacon until crisp. Put in slow cooker. Pepper the beef, add to skillet and sear on each side for 2–3 minutes. Transfer beef to slow cooker.
Add red wine to skillet, scraping down bits. Allow to simmer and reduce. Slowly add chicken stock, tomato sauce and soy sauce. Slowly whisk in flour. Add sauce to slow cooker.
Add garlic, thyme, carrots, potatoes and mushrooms to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cook on low until tender, 8–10 hours.
Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Pulled Pork with BBQ Sauce (Slow Cooker)

steps.text: Mix the rub together, then rub all over the pork.
Place in a slow cooker and pour over apple juice. Slow cook on low for 10 hours. Pork should be tender enough to shred easily.
Browning in oven (optional, recommended): preheat oven to 180 °C.
Transfer pork from slow cooker into a roasting pan. Reserve liquid.
Scoop fat off the surface of the juices in the slow cooker and drizzle over pork (about 1/3 cup), then roast pork for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven, cut thick layer of fat off top and discard. Spoon over 1/4 cup fat from slow cooker juices, then roast 15 minutes.
Shredding: shred pork using 2 forks. Pour over BBQ sauce and toss gently.
BBQ sauce: place all ingredients in a saucepan and simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 45 minutes or until thickened.
Add 3/4–1 cup of juices from the slow cooker until sauce is a syrup consistency.
Adjust to taste: sweetness with brown sugar/honey, salt, and sour with vinegar. Use per recipe.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken (Dump Bag Option)

ingredients.heading: To add at end of cooking
To serve
items: Rice, chopped spring onion, sesame seeds

steps.text: Put everything (except cornflour) into slow cooker and stir.
Cook with lid on for 4 hours on High or at least 6 hours on Low.
When chicken is tender and falling apart, scoop out a couple of tablespoons of the liquid and mix into the cornflour in a small bowl. Whisk until totally smooth and add back into the chicken mixture.
Gently shred the chicken with 2 forks and stir thoroughly so that the cornflour is distributed.
If sauce does not thicken, leave in slow cooker on High for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve sprinkled with chopped spring onion and sesame seeds.

notes: Dump bag prep – put all raw ingredients into a storage bag and freeze. Defrost overnight (or more) in the fridge, then dump all into the slow cooker.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Apricot Chicken
recipes.yield: Serves 4 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 5 hrs 20 mins

items: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into thirds
40 g sachet French onion soup mix
410 g can apricot halves in juice, drained

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Brown half the chicken for 3 minutes each side, then move to a 5.5 L slow cooker. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken.
Cook the onion in the same pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the soup mix, nectar, mustard and ginger, then pour into the slow cooker and add the thyme.
Cover and cook on low for 5 hours, adding the apricot halves for the last 20 minutes.
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl with 1 cup boiling water, cover and stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, stir in the parsley and season.
Serve the chicken on the couscous with broccolini, scattered with almonds.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooked Herb & Garlic Lamb Forequarter Chops

steps.text: Season chops with salt and pepper. In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb chops on both sides until browned, about 2–3 minutes per side.
Place onion, carrots and potatoes at the bottom of the slow cooker.
In a small bowl, mix together the minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, parsley, lemon juice and lemon zest.
Place chops on top of the vegetables in the slow cooker. Pour the garlic and herb mixture over the lamb chops. Add the broth and wine.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 hours or high for 3–4 hours, until the lamb is tender.
Serve lamb chops and vegetables, spooning over some cooking juices for added flavour.

items: 850 g beef chuck steak, cut into 5 cm pieces
40 g pkt French onion soup mix

steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan/Dutch oven pot over high heat.
Cook beef, in batches, for 5 minutes or until browned. Transfer to a large heatproof bowl.
Add onion and carrot to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes or until golden.
Return beef to the pan with tomato paste. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute to combine.
Add stock, soup mix and 1 thyme sprig. Bring to the boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1 1/2 hours or until the beef is tender.
Meanwhile, make mashed potato: cook potato in boiling water and drain. Add butter and milk and mash.
Serve over mash, sprinkled with extra thyme leaves.

recipes.title: Braised Beef with Red Wine & Vegetables
recipes.yield: Serves 6 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 3 hrs 40 mins

items: 1.4 kg beef blade roast, trimmed, cut into 3 cm pieces
3/4 cup (185 ml) red wine (or extra beef stock)
3 thyme sprigs, plus extra to serve
2 carrots, peeled, cut into 2 cm pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (140 °C fan).
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium–high heat and cook the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp. Lift into a large (2.3 L) ovenproof dish with a slotted spoon.
Season the beef and brown it in two batches, about 6 minutes each, then add to the dish.
Leave 1 Tbsp fat in the pan. Over medium heat, cook the mushrooms, onion and garlic for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the tomato paste for 1 minute, then the flour for 1 minute. Add the wine, stock and thyme and bring to a simmer.
Pour into the dish, cover with foil and bake for 2 1/4–2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender.
Uncover, stir in the carrot and bake 45 minutes more until tender. Discard the thyme, season, and skim off any fat.
Serve with mashed potato and extra thyme.

notes: Freezes for up to 1 month. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat covered at 160 °C for 50–60 minutes, stirring halfway.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Beef Brisket with BBQ Sauce

items: 1 Tbsp olive oil (or vegetable or canola oil)

ingredients.heading: BBQ sauce
items: 2 tsp each black pepper, onion powder and mustard powder

steps.text: Mix the rub and coat the brisket. If you have time, refrigerate for 30 minutes to 24 hours.
Stir the BBQ sauce ingredients together in the slow cooker, then add the brisket, pressing it down into the sauce.
Cook on low for 8 hours (1.5 kg) to 10 hours (2 kg). Lift the brisket onto a tray.
Pour the slow cooker liquid into a saucepan and simmer over medium–high heat until reduced to a syrupy sauce.
Drizzle the brisket with oil and roast at 200 °C for 15 minutes until browned in spots.
Baste generously with sauce and roast 5 minutes; repeat; then baste once more and roast 5–10 minutes until caramelised.
Slice thinly across the grain and serve with the remaining sauce.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Beef Pot Roast
recipes.yield: Serves 8 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 8 hrs 20 mins

items: 1 large onion, cut into large dice
5 carrots, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm pieces
3 celery stalks, cut into 4 cm pieces
250 ml dry red wine (or beef broth)
750 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm pieces

steps.text: Pat the beef dry and season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over high heat and brown the beef well all over, about 7 minutes. Move it to the slow cooker.
In the same pan, cook the onion and garlic for about 2 minutes until browned. Add the wine, let it reduce by half, then tip into the slow cooker.
Mix the flour with about 1 cup of the broth (a few lumps are fine) and pour in, then add the remaining broth, carrot, celery, rosemary and thyme.
Cover and cook on low for 5 hours. Add the potatoes and cook on low for 3 hours more.
Rest the beef for 5 minutes, then slice thickly. Season the sauce and serve the beef with the vegetables and plenty of sauce.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Cajun Beef Brisket with Kidney Beans
recipes.yield: Serves 8 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 4 hrs 30 mins

items: 510 g jar tomato and basil pasta sauce
2 x 420 g cans red kidney beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Cut the beef into 4 even pieces and season with pepper. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium–high heat and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes each, turning once. Move to the slow cooker.
Pour the pasta sauce into the pan. Add 1 cup (250 ml) water to the empty jar, shake and add to the pan with the spice mix. Bring to a simmer.
Pour over the beef. Cover and cook on high for 4 hours (or low for 8 hours) until very tender. (Or roast, tightly covered, at 150 °C for 3–4 hours.)
Cool the beef slightly on a plate, then shred with two forks into a large bowl.
Spoon the fat off the cooking liquid, stir 2–3 cups (500–750 ml) of the liquid through the beef and season.
Stir in the beans. Serve topped with fetta, yoghurt and coriander, with the wraps.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezer for 3 months. Black beans work instead of kidney beans.

steps.text: Lamb: add the chopped vegetables and a sprig of rosemary to the slow cooker. Sprinkle over 3 Tbsp of cornflour.
Using a small sharp knife, poke holes in the lamb at regular intervals. Press a small sprig of rosemary and a slice of garlic clove into each hole. Season lamb well with salt and pepper.

Place the lamb shoulder into the slow cooker and pour the stock and wine down the sides, taking care not to wash the seasoning off the top of the lamb. Lamb should sit in liquid with approximately half to two-thirds covered. If not, move some vegetables around or add more stock and wine.

Cook on low for five and a half hours, or four on high. Once cooked, remove the lamb, place it on a roasting dish, and cook in the oven for 20 minutes at 190 °C. Whilst the lamb is cooking in the oven, prepare the gravy.
Gravy: remove fat from juices in slow cooker.
Transfer contents of slow cooker to a saucepan. Add a further tablespoon of cornflour (make a slurry with a few tablespoons of liquid).
Bring the gravy to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Add a teaspoon of blackcurrant jam, then check the thickness and reduce further if required.
Check the seasoning, then serve by pouring through a colander into a gravy jug.

items: 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced diagonally
1 large onion, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cm x 2 cm piece ginger, grated

steps.text: Prepare all the ingredients as above.
Place the chicken at the bottom of the slow cooker. Add all the remaining ingredients on top of the chicken, except for the spring onions and sesame seeds.
Cook on low for 6 hours.
Serve with rice and sprinkle with spring onions and sesame seeds evenly on top.

items: 2 large spring onions, white parts minced, green parts sliced
3 cups (750 ml) apple purée (the book misprints this as "3/4 cup 3 cups" – 750 ml matches 3 cups)
800 g beef short ribs on the bone

steps.text: Mix everything except the ribs and the sliced green spring onion in a large bowl.
Put the ribs in a sealable container and coat well with the marinade.
Seal and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Preheat the oven to 150 °C.
Put the ribs in a deep-sided baking tray and bake for 3 hours until dark, sticky and tender.
Serve hot, garnished with the sliced spring onion.

recipes.title: Silverside (On-Stove)
recipes.source: Recipe based on australianbeef.com.au and cookingperfected.com

steps.text: Rinse beef in cold water. Place into a pot and cover with cold water.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 2 hours, maintaining a simmer.
Once cooked, remove from heat and let rest in pot (or out). Serve.

notes: Allow 25–30 minutes cooking time for each 500 g of beef.

recipes.title: Poulet Rôti (French Roast Chicken with Potatoes)
recipes.yield: Serves 4 | Prep 40 mins | Cook 1 hr 10 mins

ingredients.heading: Potatoes
items: 750 g starchy potatoes, peeled, cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 210 °C (190 °C fan) with a 28 cm cast-iron pot (no lid) inside. Let the chicken sit out to take the chill off.
Mix the butter, herbes de Provence, salt and garlic.
Pat the chicken dry. Gently loosen the skin over the breasts, thighs and drumsticks with a spoon. Spread two-thirds of the butter under the breast skin and the rest under the leg skin.
Season the cavity with 1/4 tsp salt, the herbes de Provence and thyme. Tie the legs, rub the chicken with oil, season the outside with the remaining salt and tuck the wings under.
Toss the potatoes and whole garlic with the salt, pepper and oil.
Carefully take out the hot pot, spread the potatoes over the base and sit the chicken on top. Cover loosely with foil and roast 30 minutes.
Remove the foil, baste, and roast uncovered for 40 minutes, basting twice more, until the thigh reaches 72 °C.
Rest the chicken in the pot on its side for 15 minutes, basting once more.
Carve (don't miss the two "oysters" on the back) and serve with the potatoes, pan juices and fresh thyme.

recipes.title: Crispy Herb Baked Chicken with Gravy

items: 1 Tbsp vegetable oil (canola or peanut – not butter or olive oil)

ingredients.heading: Chicken (choose one)
items: 1.8 kg bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

ingredients.heading: Herb rub
items: 1 tsp dried sage (or 1/2 tsp ground sage)
1 tsp coarse/kosher salt (or 1 3/4 tsp sea salt flakes)

ingredients.heading: Gravy
items: 3/4 tsp dark soy sauce or gravy browner

steps.text: Optional: pat the skin dry and refrigerate uncovered overnight for extra-crisp skin.
Preheat the oven to 240 °C (220 °C fan). Line a tray with foil then baking paper and set a rack on top.

Mix the herb rub. Pat the chicken dry, rub with oil, then coat with the rub, working it into the crevices. Place on the rack skin side up (a butterflied chicken breast side up, tail towards the back of the oven).
Roast pieces for 35 minutes (to 75 °C), or a butterflied chicken for 45 minutes (breast 66 °C, leg joint 75 °C). Grill on high for 1–3 minutes if the skin needs more crisping.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 5 minutes.

Gravy: scrape all the juices, fat and browned bits from the tray into a saucepan. Heat over medium until bubbling, whisk in the flour, then slowly whisk in the stock. Add the soy sauce and pepper and stir 3–5 minutes until syrupy. Season.
Carve the chicken and serve with the gravy.

items: 1.25 kg bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and/or drumsticks

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Mix the seasoning.
Put the chicken in a 23 x 33 cm baking dish, rub with oil and then the seasoning (mostly on the skin). Arrange skin side up.
Whisk the flour with about 1/2 cup stock until smooth, then whisk in the rest of the stock and the pepper. Pour around (not over) the chicken.
Bake uncovered for 50 minutes until the chicken is golden and crisp.
Move the chicken to a plate. Whisk the gravy smooth, adjust thickness with a little water if needed, season, and serve with the chicken.

ingredients.heading: Seasoning
items: 1 tsp dried oregano or thyme (or other herb)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan).
Pound the chicken to an even 1.5 cm at the thickest part. Mix the seasoning.
Line a tray with foil and baking paper. Lay the chicken upside down, rub with 1 tsp oil and sprinkle with seasoning. Flip and repeat on the other side.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and cooked through (75 °C inside).
Move straight onto plates and rest 3–5 minutes. Garnish with parsley.

ingredients.heading: Chicken
items: 500 g chicken tenderloins (or breast cut lengthwise into 1.5 cm slices)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).
Spread the panko on a tray, spray lightly with oil and bake 3–5 minutes until light golden. Tip into a bowl.
Set a rack on a baking tray if you have one (for more even baking).
Whisk the batter ingredients with a fork, add the chicken and toss to coat.
Lift each piece into the toasted panko, sprinkle more over the top and press to stick, then place on the tray.
Spray lightly with oil, sprinkle with a little salt and bake 15 minutes (up to 20 for larger pieces).
Serve straight away with dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmigiana
recipes.yield: Serves 6 | Prep 20 mins + 30 mins brining | Cook 40 mins

ingredients.heading: Brined chicken
items: 3 chicken breasts (about 300 g each), halved horizontally into 6 pieces
1 tsp cooking/kosher salt (or 3/4 tsp table salt)

ingredients.heading: Frying
items: 2 cups (about 480 ml) olive, vegetable or canola oil

ingredients.heading: Parmigiana sauce
items: 1/4 cup (about 40 g) finely chopped onion or eschalots

steps.text: Dry brine: season both sides of the chicken with the salt, pepper and herbs and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Sauce: heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the garlic and onion for about 3 minutes. Stir in the chilli and herbs for 15 seconds. Add the wine and simmer on higher heat until mostly evaporated. Add the passata, stock, salt and pepper, cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes until thickened.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Set up three shallow bowls: flour, beaten egg mixture, and crumb mixture. Coat each piece in flour, dip in egg, then press into the crumbs.
Heat 1.5–2 cm oil in a skillet over medium–high heat (180 °C). Fry 2–3 pieces at a time, 2 minutes on the first side and 1 1/2 minutes on the second. Drain on a rack.
Place the chicken on a baking tray. Spoon about 1/3 cup sauce over most of each piece, leaving the edges bare so they stay crisp.
Top with basil, plenty of mozzarella and parmesan, and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake 15 minutes until the cheese is melted with a few brown spots – no longer.
Serve straight away with extra basil and any leftover sauce.

items: Sesame seeds and green onion, for serving

steps.text: Preheat oven to 218 °C. Spray oil in a baking dish.
Place drumsticks in a single layer on prepared pan.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sriracha and ground ginger. Pour over the drumsticks.
Bake 40 minutes, flipping halfway through, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 74 °C.
Remove chicken from oven and turn broiler/grill on.
Pour the sauce from the pan into a small saucepan. Set over medium heat and bring to a simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk together cornstarch with 1 Tbsp of cold water.
Pour the cornstarch mixture into the sauce mixture and whisk to combine. The sauce will thicken quickly; remove it as soon as it thickens.
Brush the thickened sauce over the chicken and return to the oven. Watch closely – leave in for just a few minutes, until the sauce is glossy.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced green onions before serving.

recipes.title: Juiciest Baked Pork Tenderloin

steps.text: Preheat your oven to 204 °C. Dry the pork tenderloins well with paper towels.
Mix the paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper together in a small bowl. Rub this spice mix over all sides of the pork.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the pork, working in 2 batches if your pan is not big enough to fit both tenderloins without them touching. Sear the pork on all sides until it is brown, about 6 minutes total. Take the pan off the heat.

Move the pork to a baking dish. If the spices left in the pan are black, wipe them away with a paper towel. Return the pan to the heat and add the beef broth. Scrape the bottom of the pan to remove any stuck-on bits, then boil for 1 minute until it reduces to about 1/4 cup. Pour this sauce over the pork.
Pour the apple cider vinegar over the pork, then dot the top with the butter. Cover the baking dish with foil.

Bake the pork for 20–25 minutes, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 145 °F (63 °C). Let the pork rest for 5 minutes before slicing into 1/4-inch-thick rounds. Pour leftover sauce over the meat.

notes: Pork will be a tiny bit pink in the centre.

recipes.title: Juicy Stove Top Chicken – Seasoning Rub

steps.text: Season both sides of the chicken: grease chicken with oil and season with salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika and dried basil.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken to pan. Do not stir or move chicken while cooking. Cook for 5–7 minutes.
Flip the chicken over. Add a tablespoon of butter to the pan. Cook for 7 more minutes (or until cooked through).
Let chicken rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes, then slice and serve.

recipes.title: Maple Glazed Ham
recipes.source: Cafe Delites (cafedelites.com) – method summarised; converted to metric
recipes.yield: Serves 25–30 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 1 hr 15 mins

items: 3.6–4.5 kg (8–10 lb) bone-in, fully cooked ham

steps.text: Let the ham sit at room temperature for 1–2 hours. Preheat the oven to 150 °C with a rack in the lower third. Line a baking dish with foil or baking paper.

Remove the rind, leaving the fat. Score the fat in a 2.5 cm diamond pattern no more than 6 mm deep. Put the ham in the dish, pour the pineapple juice and water into the base, cover and bake 30 minutes.

Glaze: heat the butter in a saucepan over medium heat until golden brown. Add the sugar, maple syrup, mustard, cinnamon and cloves and stir about 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves. Turn to low, add the garlic and bring to a simmer. Cool to lukewarm.
Increase the oven to 220 °C. Uncover the ham, brush with a third of the glaze (into the cuts too) and bake uncovered 15 minutes.
Brush with another third plus some pan juices and bake 15 minutes; repeat until there's a dark golden crust (about 30 minutes in total). Mix pan juices into the glaze if it gets too thick to brush.
If needed, grill for 2–5 minutes to finish the crust, watching closely.
Rest 10–20 minutes before slicing.

ingredients.heading: Topping
items: 1.2 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic and cook for 1 minute. Then add carrots and celery. Cook for 3 minutes or until softened and sweet.
Turn heat up to high. Add beef and cook, breaking it up as you go, until browned.
Add flour and mix in. Add tomato paste, beef stock, red wine/water, stock powder, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, bay leaves, salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, then turn down heat so it is simmering rapidly. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it reduces down to a gravy consistency. Taste, then add more salt if desired.
Transfer to a 1.5 litre pie dish. Allow to cool a bit.
Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Cook potatoes in boiling water for 15 minutes or until soft. Drain, then return to the pot on the turned-off stove. Shake briefly and allow to steam dry for 30 seconds or so.
Add butter and mash until melted, then add milk and salt. Mash until smooth.
Spread onto pie and use a fork to rough up the surface (rougher surface = more golden bits). Sprinkle with parmesan and drizzle with melted butter.
Bake for 25–30 minutes or until golden on top and bubbling on the edges. Stick a knife into the middle to ensure it is piping hot.
Stand for 5 minutes before serving.

items: 500 g golden delight potatoes, peeled and cubed
4 sheets frozen ready-rolled puff pastry, partially thawed

steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add half the lamb. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes or until browned. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with 1 Tbsp oil and remaining lamb.

Heat remaining oil in pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic. Cook, stirring, for 3 minutes or until soft. Add potatoes and carrots. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until browned. Add tomato paste and gravy powder. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute.

Return lamb to pan. Add stock and Worcestershire sauce. Increase heat to high. Bring to the boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, stirring occasionally, for 2 hours or until lamb is tender. Stir in rosemary. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cornflour and 2 Tbsp warm water. Add to lamb mixture. Simmer for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Prepare pastry for pies. Divide lamb mixture between pastry cases. Cook using a pie maker. Allow pies to stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Cheesy Tuna and Potato Pie (for Pie Maker)
recipes.source: Recipe adapted from a Women's Weekly cookbook

items: Frozen ready-rolled shortcrust pastry sheets or puff pastry
185 g can tuna in brine, drained and flaked
1 tsp chopped fresh dill (or other similar herb)

steps.text: Cut potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Boil, steam or microwave potatoes until tender; drain.
Melt butter in a large pan, add flour and cook, stirring, until bubbling. Remove from heat and gradually stir in milk. Stir over heat until mixture boils and thickens.
Stir in potatoes, cheese, mustard, tuna and herbs; cool.
Prepare pies in a pie maker.

recipes.title: Beef Sausage Rolls (Using Beef Sausage Mince)

items: 3 puff pastry sheets, defrosted and sliced in half

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Sauté the onions for a few minutes until translucent. Allow to cool.
In a small bowl, whisk the egg and add the milk to make the egg wash.
Place beef sausage mince in a large mixing bowl. Add half the egg wash, cooked onions, breadcrumbs, thyme, pepper, garlic salt and soy sauce. Mix well to combine and form into a large ball.

Place equal portions of beef mixture across the middle of each sheet of puff pastry. Fold the right-hand side of the pastry over the mince, brush the top and open side with leftover egg wash, then continue to roll up.
Place sausage roll on a lined baking tray (seal side down), then baste with remaining egg wash. [Freeze here if preparing ahead.]
Optional: partially slice sausage rolls.
Bake for around 30–40 minutes or until meat is cooked and pastry is flaky and golden brown.

recipes.title: Quiche

steps.text: Line a pie dish with shortcrust pastry. Cook the shell before filling (blind baking).
Cook onion in butter.
Blend in flour, salt and pepper.
Add cream, whisking until smooth and thickened.
Cool slightly. Mix eggs in a large bowl.
Gradually add cream mixture to eggs while whisking.
Stir in spinach, bacon and grated cheese.
Pour mixture into crust and bake for 20–25 minutes.

notes: Can add other veges, e.g. mushroom, capsicum, zucchini etc.

steps.text: Trim rind off bacon and chop finely.
Finely chop onion and grate zucchini.
Place all ingredients in a bowl (except eggs).
Beat eggs lightly and stir into mix.
Pour into a well-greased tin (11 x 7 inch tin).
Bake in a moderate oven (180 °C) for 30–40 minutes or until brown.

recipes.title: Basic Chicken and Sweet Corn Soup

steps.text: Place chicken stock in a large saucepan with the soy sauce, ginger and creamed corn.
Bring to a boil (simmer).
Add the chicken and green onion and cook for 3–4 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.
Serve sprinkled with extra chopped green onion, with bread.

recipes.title: Potato and Leek Soup with Pancetta/Bacon

items: (Can also add 400 g broccoli with the potatoes)

steps.text: Cook pancetta/bacon in a saucepan until crisp. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel.

Melt the butter in the pan (medium saucepan). Cook the leek, stirring, for 3 minutes or until soft. Add potato, stock and half the pancetta/bacon. Bring to the boil. Simmer, covered, for 5–10 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Cool slightly. Use a stick blender to blend until smooth.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Drizzle with the cream and top with remaining pancetta/bacon.

items: 3 sprigs of thyme, plus extra to serve
1 cup risoni or other small pasta
Grated parmesan and crusty bread, to serve

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan/pot on medium. Sauté leek, bacon, thyme and rosemary for 4–5 minutes.
Add carrots and garlic. Sauté for 2–3 minutes until golden. Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add stock, water and risoni. Bring to the boil. Reduce to low and simmer for 10–15 minutes until pasta is al dente.
Remove herb sprigs. Serve soup topped with parmesan and extra thyme. Accompany with bread.

items: 1 cup white kidney beans, drained and rinsed
3/4 cup frozen corn kernels (can use peas and corn)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Place leftover hambone in a large stockpot or Dutch oven and add enough water to cover the bone halfway, about 6–7 cups. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until very fragrant, about 30 minutes to 1 hour. Set aside ham stock and discard hambone.
Heat olive oil in the large stockpot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add garlic, onion, carrots and potato. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions have become translucent, about 2–3 minutes.
Stir in ham stock, beans, corn, thyme and bay leaves; season with salt and pepper, to taste.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 10–12 minutes. Stir in ham until heated through, about 1–2 minutes.
Serve immediately.

ingredients.heading: Soup
items: 1/2 tsp white sugar, or more (only if needed)
1/2 cup cream (optional), plus extra for drizzling (or 30 g butter)
1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped (optional)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan).
Toss the tomatoes and whole garlic with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper. Lay the tomatoes cut side up on a tray and roast for 40–45 minutes until charred in spots.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium–high heat and cook the minced garlic and onion for about 3 minutes until soft.
Add the roasted tomatoes and juices, squeeze in the roasted garlic flesh and add the stock. Blend until smooth.
Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, add sugar only if it tastes too sharp, then stir in the cream.
Serve drizzled with cream and topped with basil – great with grilled cheese sandwiches.

ingredients.heading: Soup
items: 250 g peeled garlic cloves (50–60 cloves, about 5 bulbs), roughly chopped
1 small brown onion (or 1/2 large), diced small
1.5 kg starchy potato, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
2 tsp cooking/kosher salt (halve for table salt)

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based pot over medium–high heat. Cook the garlic for 5 minutes, stirring often, until golden at the edges but not deeply browned.
Add the onion and cook 2 minutes, then the potato for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to high, add the stock, water, salt and pepper. Once simmering, reduce to medium and cook uncovered for 15 minutes until the potato is soft.
Stir in the cream and simmer 1 minute. Take off the heat and blend until completely smooth. Adjust thickness with water and season to taste.
Garnish: toast the panko with the oil and salt in a small frying pan over medium–high heat, stirring, for about 3 minutes until golden. Stir in the parsley.
Serve the soup hot, topped with the crunchy crumbs.

recipes.title: Creamy Cauliflower Soup

items: 1 kg (1 medium head) cauliflower, florets and roughly chopped stalk
250 g potatoes (1 large or 2 small), peeled and roughly diced
To garnish (optional): fresh thyme, cream and/or olive oil

steps.text: Put everything except the salt and pepper in a large pot and bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce to medium and simmer 10–15 minutes until the cauliflower is very soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
Thin with extra milk, water or stock if needed, or simmer longer to thicken.
Serve with thyme leaves and a drizzle of cream or olive oil.

notes: If using a countertop blender, let the soup cool first, then reheat after blending.

recipes.title: Hen's Soup with Double Dumplings (Danish)

ingredients.heading: Soup stock
items: 2 leeks, white part only, halved lengthways, then thinly sliced
Bouquet garni of thyme, parsley and bay leaf (optional)

ingredients.heading: Meatballs
items: 2 slices white bread, crusts discarded, bread torn

steps.text: Stock: put the chicken in a large saucepan, cover with water and bring to the boil over high heat. Drain, discarding the liquid, and rinse the chicken under running water to remove any scum.
Return the chicken to the cleaned pan, cover with fresh water and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the remaining stock ingredients, then simmer on low for 1 hour, skimming off scum as it rises.
Remove the chicken and bouquet garni. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the stock (and the chicken) for another use if you like – the book pairs it with asparagus tartlets.

Dumplings: bring 1 cup (250 ml) water to the boil in a small saucepan. Melt in the butter, then take off the heat. Stir in the flour and salt until smooth, then beat in the eggs one at a time until well combined. Transfer to a bowl and rest for 20 minutes.
Meatballs: pulse all the meatball ingredients in a food processor until just combined.
Shape the meatball mixture into 2 cm balls, and do the same with the dumpling dough. Refrigerate until ready to cook.
Bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a simmer. Cook the meatballs first, then the dumplings, in batches, just until they float (1–2 minutes each batch). Remove with a slotted spoon.
Divide the dumplings and meatballs among bowls and ladle over the hot soup and vegetables.

notes: An older boiling chicken gives a stronger-flavoured soup than a young roasting bird.

recipes.title: Buttery Seasoned Rice

items: 50 g (3 Tbsp) butter, to stir through

steps.text: Place all rice ingredients (except butter) in a large saucepan and give it a stir.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat (edges bubbling, entire surface rippling), put the lid on and turn stove down to medium-low (low for strong stoves). It should be simmering gently.
Cook for 13 minutes – do not lift lid.
Tilt pot, then quickly peek to ensure all water is absorbed.
Remove from stove and stand for 10 minutes with lid on.
Add butter and fluff rice with a rubber spatula.

notes: Rice cooker – same ingredients, water and rice ratio.

items: 1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed in a sieve and drained

steps.text: Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and sauté until starting to deepen in colour, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and sauté until just barely starting to deepen in colour, about 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock and season with salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil.
Add rice and stir once, cover with a snug lid, then reduce heat to low. Let simmer until liquid has been absorbed, about 15–18 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest 5–10 minutes. Add remaining 3 Tbsp butter, toss and fluff with a fork.
Serve warm, garnished with parsley.

items: 2 cups frozen corn (no need to thaw) or fresh kernels
1 cup uncooked long-grain rice, not rinsed
1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken stock (plus 2 Tbsp if using fresh corn)

steps.text: Use a small pot or saucepan about 20–22 cm wide.
Melt half the butter over high heat. Stir the garlic for 15 seconds, then add the corn and half the salt and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir 30 seconds. Add the stock, remaining salt and pepper. Once the whole surface is bubbling, cover and turn to medium–low.
Cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid or stirring, then take off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining butter, fluff the rice until it melts, and toss through the green onion.
In a large saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil.
Add the rice and stir to coat the grains with oil.
Add a splash of tomato sauce and a pinch of cumin.
Add the chicken stock and tomatoes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer until cooked (about 25 minutes).
Stir through about a tablespoon of butter and serve.

items: 1 Tbsp lemon juice (or 1 tsp apple cider vinegar)
3 cups low-sodium vegetable or chicken stock

steps.text: Trim the root and dark green tops from the leeks, halve lengthwise and slice into half-moons. Swish in cold water to remove grit and drain on a towel.
Heat the oil and butter in a large wide pot over medium–high heat. Sauté the leeks for 3–4 minutes until soft and lightly golden, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, salt, pepper and lemon juice. Add the stock, scraping up any browned bits, and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer 18–22 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Take off the heat and stir through the parmesan and cheddar. Serve warm with extra cheese or parsley.

recipes.title: Sun-Dried Tomato and Basil Rice with Chicken Schnitzel

items: 1/2 cup (75 g) chopped drained sun-dried tomatoes, 1 Tbsp oil reserved

steps.text: Cook the schnitzels following packet directions. Slice.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes or until aromatic. Add the stock and rice and stir to combine. Bring to the boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Shred 1/4 cup basil. Add to the rice mixture with the parmesan, tomato and reserved oil. Gently toss to combine. Season.
Divide rice mixture among serving plates. Top with the schnitzel and remaining basil leaves to serve.

items: Garlic salt (or crushed garlic and salt)

steps.text: Boil potatoes with skins until just soft, then drain.
Place on a tray and squash (e.g. with a potato masher or glass).
Leave to steam for about 5 minutes.
Drizzle potatoes with melted butter and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Roast in oven at 180 °C for about 40 minutes.

recipes.title: Double-Sided Hasselback Potatoes

items: 1 kg small potatoes, such as Dutch cream or kipfler, peeled
1 tsp salt, plus extra for seasoning
150 ml sunflower oil or other mild-flavoured vegetable oil

steps.text: Lay a chopstick on a chopping board with a potato right beside it. Using the chopstick as a stopper, slice the potato two-thirds of the way through at a 45° angle, in slices 1–2 mm apart.

Turn the potato over so the cuts face down and repeat on the other side at the same angle, so the two sets of cuts cross each other – the potato stays in one piece. Repeat with the remaining potatoes.
Put the potatoes in a large saucepan of cold water with the salt and vinegar. Bring to a simmer over medium–high heat, cook for 15 minutes, then drain gently and leave to air dry for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Place the potatoes in a roasting tin. Mix the butter and oil, drizzle generously over the potatoes, toss gently and season well with salt.
Roast for 45 minutes–1 hour, turning gently a few times, until crisp and well browned. Season with more salt if needed.

notes: Instead of a chopstick, you can sit the potato against the edge of a thin chopping board placed on a larger one to stop the knife. The salt and vinegar help the potatoes hold together, but still handle them gently.

items: 1 kg potatoes, cut into thin wedge shapes/slices
Salt and pepper, to taste (can even add chives)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C. Grease a large baking dish.
Partially cook the potatoes in a pot of water on the stove.
Meanwhile, sauté onions and bacon in a frypan. Add garlic and stir for a minute. Turn off heat, add creams and half the cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a large baking dish, line and layer half the potato. Pour over half the onion-cream mixture. Layer the remaining potato on top and then the onion-cream mixture. Garnish with remaining cheese.
Cover dish with foil and bake in oven for 30–40 minutes. Remove foil, then bake for a further 20–30 minutes.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Chips

items: 700 g (approx.) floury potatoes, sliced about 1 cm thick

steps.text: Add chips to a bowl and toss with cornflour until coated.
Add oil, salt, pepper and paprika and toss again so they're evenly coated.
Place in the air fryer and cook at 190 °C for 20 minutes, shaking chips every 5 minutes.

notes: If using more than 700 g of chips, you may need to cook them in 2 batches.

To freeze chips: wash chips/sliced potatoes. Blanch in boiling water for 2–5 minutes, then place in an ice bath. Dry well. Arrange sliced potatoes on a tray lined with baking paper. Flash freeze for about 1 hour, then place into freezer bags. To cook, follow the steps above.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200–210 °C.
Use a fork to poke a few holes in the potatoes.
Rub potatoes with oil and sprinkle liberally with salt (and pepper).
Bake for 45–60 minutes until fork-tender.
Preheat oven to 220 °C. Line/grease a tray or casserole dish.
Cut carrots into thirds (or as desired – even pieces).
Melt butter in a pan. Pour in honey and cook while stirring until completely melted through the butter. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, while stirring.
Add the carrots and allow sauce to thicken for a further minute while tossing the carrots through the sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer carrots to tray in a single layer. Roast for 20 minutes or until fork-tender.

items: 2 Tbsp chopped parsley or spring onions

steps.text: Wipe mushrooms. Halve or quarter if large.
Chop garlic and cook gently in a frypan in butter.
Stir in soy sauce and cornflour, then toss in mushrooms.
Cook for 5–6 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley or spring onions.
Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Place zucchini in a bowl. Add a bit of salt. Drizzle over olive oil and stir to coat.
Mix panko, parmesan, salt, pepper, oregano and garlic powder in a small bowl.
Dip zucchini in breadcrumbs to cover and place onto baking sheet.
Bake until zucchini chips are tender and cheese is browned (about 15 minutes – but probably longer, and may need the grill).

recipes.title: Basic Stir-Fried Bok Choy
recipes.source: Recipe from The Woks of Life

items: About 1 kg fresh bok choy/pak choy

steps.text: Slice (at a slight angle) and wash bok choy.
Heat wok/large pan over low heat and add the oil. Immediately add the ginger first (if using), then garlic.
Add bok choy and turn up heat to the highest setting. Stir-fry using a scooping motion to distribute ginger, garlic and oil, for around 30 seconds.
Next add salt, sugar, sesame oil, white pepper and hot chicken stock. Stir-fry for 1–2 minutes. Plate and serve immediately.

notes: Can add other veggies like carrot and onion.

items: 3–4 Tbsp liquid (milk, liquid from can etc.)

steps.text: Beat egg, liquid and corn together.
Add flour and baking powder to the bowl and stir with a fork. Do not over-mix.
Add more liquid if needed.
Cook in a non-stick pan with a bit of butter.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Add onions and stir to coat in butter.
Place lid on skillet and leave for 20 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Remove lid, then cook for a further 20 minutes, stirring every now and then, until onion is golden (increase heat slightly if the colour is not changing).
Add sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper. Cook for a further 10 minutes until jammy.
Remove from heat and keep warm.
In a saucepan, melt the butter.
Add the flour and stir together.
Pour in about 1 cup milk.
Cook, stirring, until the right consistency.
Add in grated cheese and a sprinkle of garlic salt.

items: Diced mushroom and onion (2 mushrooms, 1/4 onion)

steps.text: In a saucepan, melt the butter.
Add diced mushroom and onion. Cook gently until softened.
Add the flour.
Pour in about 1 cup milk or cream.
Cook, stirring, until the right consistency.
Add salt or garlic salt.

items: 1/2 tsp onion powder (optional, or garlic powder)

steps.text: Dissolve the stock cubes in the boiling water.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then stir in the flour, onion powder and pepper.
Slowly whisk in half the stock until smooth, then add the rest.
Stir for 1 1/2–2 minutes until thickened to gravy consistency. Season and serve.
Dissolve 1 tsp sugar in 1 Tbsp hot water.
Then add soy sauce, rice vinegar, chilli oil, minced garlic, sesame seeds and sesame oil.
Stir to combine.
Combine the ingredients in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Stir for a few minutes until the sugar dissolves. Don't boil the mixture.
Transfer the sauce to a bottle and store in the pantry until ready to use.

recipes.title: Ginger Pickled Beets

items: 5 or 6 medium red beets (tails and about 1 inch of stem left intact)
1/2 cup thinly sliced, peeled fresh ginger (or a couple of teaspoons minced ginger)

steps.text: Cover beets with cold water by 2 inches in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil; reduce heat. Simmer beets until tender when pierced with the tip of a knife, about 30 minutes. Transfer beets with a slotted spoon to an ice-water bath. Discard cooking liquid. Trim beets and remove skins. Cut beets into very thin rounds; transfer to a large bowl/jar.

Bring ginger, vinegar, sugar and salt to a boil in a medium saucepan and stir until sugar is dissolved. Pour liquid over beets; stir. Let stand until completely cool (at least an hour) or refrigerate.

notes: Can be refrigerated for up to 1 month.

items: 250 g unsalted butter, cut into 2.5 cm cubes

steps.text: In a small/medium stainless steel saucepan, put butter in and let it melt over medium-low heat.
Leave to simmer for 10 minutes (it should start to foam at about 5 minutes, then clear at 7 minutes).
Ghee is ready when the milk solids that settle on the base of the pan turn golden.
Strain through a mesh colander lined with a single sheet of paper towel.
Pour into a jar for storage. Keeps in the pantry for 3 months and the fridge for 1 year.

recipes.title: Breadmaker Dough Recipes
introNotes: Quantities are given for 450 g, 680 g and 900 g loaves.
notes: Tangzhong – for a white 900 g loaf: 30 g bread flour and 150 g water.

items: 4 cups (US) bread flour [946.36 ml, or approx. 3 3/4 Australian cups]

steps.text: In the bread machine pan, put all ingredients in the order suggested by the manufacturer.
Select the dough setting.
When cycle is complete, turn dough onto a lightly floured surface.
Divide dough into 24 portions.
Shape dough into balls.
Place in a greased 13 x 9 inch baking tray/pan.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 30–45 minutes.
Bake at 175–180 °C for 13–16 minutes or until golden brown.

items: 6 Tbsp olive oil (or other neutral oil)

steps.text: Place ingredients into the machine as per manufacturer's instructions (milk – egg – oil – sugar – salt – flour – yeast). Set machine to dough setting.
When dough is ready, place onto a lightly floured surface.

Hot dog buns: divide dough into 6–9 pieces. Roll into an oblong (oval) shape with a rolling pin. Fold dough in half and pinch edges. Fold in half again, pinch edges and tuck top and bottom ends underneath. Shape as desired. Place onto a greased tray with fold on bottom.
Burger buns: divide dough as required. Shape into firm round shapes (slightly flattened). Place onto a greased tray with folds on bottom.
Cover tray with plastic wrap and allow to rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190 °C.
Bake for 15–22 minutes, until lightly browned. Cool on a rack.

items: 240 g bread flour (215 g if using tangzhong)

ingredients.heading: Making with tangzhong – deduct these amounts from above

steps.text: Tangzhong (microwave option): mix flour and water until smooth.
Microwave on high in 15-second intervals, mixing in between, up to 45–60 seconds total. Stop when it thickens into a glossy, pudding/gravy-like paste.
Allow to cool.
Put in with the liquids in the bread machine.

ingredients.heading: Dough
items: 125 g (1/2 cup) boiled and mashed potato (about 1/2 large potato)

ingredients.heading: Rosemary topping
items: 2 1/2 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves

steps.text: Make mashed potato: peel potato and cut into 2.5 cm chunks. Boil until fully tender (10–15 minutes). Drain and mash very well. Set aside to cool, and measure out 125 g (1/2 cup).
Mix dry: place flour, salt, sugar and yeast in a large bowl and mix well with a firm spatula.
Add wet: make a well in the centre, then add olive oil and warm water. Mix with spatula until you can no longer see flour. Dough should be sticky – too sticky to knead by hand.

Add potato: add mashed potato. Using a folding motion, start mixing it through using the spatula, then start smearing it along the walls of the bowl. Once potato is evenly incorporated, shape roughly into a ball in the bowl.
Rise 1: cover bowl with cling wrap, then put in a warm place (25 °C) for 30 minutes until it increases in volume by 50% or up to double in size.

Fold dough: get another large bowl and drizzle with 2 tsp of olive oil, then smear around the bowl. Scrape dough in, then fold the edges of the dough into the centre six times. Shape into a ball and cover with cling wrap.
Rise 2: put the bowl in a warm place (25 °C) for 30 minutes until it increases in volume by 50% or doubles in size.
Prepare pan: pour in 2 Tbsp of olive oil, then smear it across the base and sides.
Preheat oven to 200 °C (fan) and set a rack on the middle shelf. Allow about 15 minutes to preheat the oven.
Put dough in pan: scrape dough into prepared pan and stretch and pull to fill the base, and get the surface roughly level.
Rise 3: cover pan with cling wrap and place in a warm place for 40 minutes.
Smear surface with oil: drizzle the surface with 2 tsp of olive oil, and smear/rub it over lightly with your hands.
Poke: using both hands like claws, push fingers deep into the dough, right to the base of the pan, to create signature dimples. Do this around half a dozen times.
Toppings: add rosemary.
Finishing olive oil and salt flakes: drizzle surface with 2 Tbsp of olive oil so it runs into the dimples. Then sprinkle with sea salt flakes.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the top is deep golden and lightly crisp, while the sides are fried and crusty.
Cool: turn out onto a cooling rack. Let rest for 10 minutes, then cut to serve.
Dissolve the sugar in warm (blood temperature) water, then sprinkle in the yeast granules.
Add the oil and then stir gently for a few seconds. Leave to stand for at least 5 minutes to allow the yeast to begin acting.
Once the yeast mixture has begun to bubble and looks a little foamy, add the remaining ingredients. Sprinkle the baking powder in evenly to prevent it forming a single lump.
Mix everything together until the dough begins to come away from the sides of the bowl and forms one large ball.
Cut dough in half and roll out to the desired shape.
Spray a pizza tray or baking tray with oil and place pizza base on tray.
Place toppings on and cook at 220 °C for 12–15 minutes.
Place dough ingredients into the bread machine in the order listed. Select the dough setting.
Remove the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Divide the dough in half and roll each into a large rectangle.
Spread pizza sauce over dough (leave a couple of cm around the edge free). Add pizza toppings.
Roll the dough up (from the longest side) into a long log. Cut into even pieces (about 8).
Place scrolls onto a baking tray, cut side up. Top with cheese. Allow scrolls to rest/rise for about 30 minutes. Optional: brush sides with egg wash.
Bake in a 180 °C fan oven for 20–25 minutes.

items: 1 1/4 cups flour, plus more to roll out
1 Tbsp dried herbs (e.g. rosemary and garlic, oregano, basil or thyme)

steps.text: Mix dry ingredients in a bowl. Add yoghurt and stir to combine. The dough will be shaggy and sticky.
Transfer to a well-floured surface and sprinkle with some flour. Fold dough in on itself a few times, then form into a ball.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and press down with your hands to form a 5-inch disc.

Heat a frying pan with enough oil to coat and prevent sticking. Lower heat to medium or medium-low and cook the flatbread for about 1 1/2 minutes on each side or until it begins to turn a nice golden brown.
Preheat oven to 200 °C.
Line a baking sheet with baking paper.
Slice bread lengthways and place open side up.
Whisk together ingredients. Spread evenly on bread.
Bake for 12 minutes (depends on the type of bread you use).

items: Optional: egg yolk whisked with a pinch of sugar and salt, for glazing

steps.text: Place flour, caster sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl and use a whisk to combine. You don't need to sift the flour.
Cut butter into 1 cm cubes and place in flour mixture.
Use a rubbing motion, like rubbing hands together, to mix the flour and butter together until you reach a breadcrumb consistency.
Add milk and use a spatula to mix into a dough.
Tip dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth (don't worry about over-kneading) and form into a ball.
Rest dough for 15–20 minutes wrapped in cling film.
Lightly flour the surface and top of the dough ball, and turn over so the smooth side is on the bench.
Roll dough in both directions until 2–2.5 cm thick and very lightly flour the top of the dough.
Cut decisively with a 6 cm round cutter, then carefully turn over the scone and place it on the tray (to create a nice sharp edge).
Optional: brush egg yolk that has been whisked with a pinch of sugar and salt neatly across the top of the scone for a golden colour.
Rest for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 180 °C fan-forced (at least 30 minutes before baking).
Bake scones for 10–11 minutes until tops are nice and golden.

recipes.title: Homemade Sesame Sea Salt Crackers
recipes.yield: Serves 5 | Prep 15 mins | Cook 22 mins + 15 mins cooling

ingredients.heading: Cracker dough
items: 1 cup plain flour, plus extra for rolling

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).
Mix the flour, sesame seeds and salt. Add the water and oil and stir until the flour is all incorporated.
Knead briefly on a lightly floured bench into a ball and cut in half.
Roll one half into an oval about 3 mm thick. Move it onto baking paper, sprinkle with half the topping seeds and salt, then roll to 2 mm thick.
Cut into 5 cm squares, leaving them in place, and slide the paper onto a tray. Repeat with the other half.
Spray with oil and bake both trays for 12 minutes. Move the browner edge pieces to the centre and bake 8–10 minutes more until all are light golden.
Cool on the trays for 15–20 minutes until crisp.

ingredients.heading: Dough
items: 1 cup milk, warmed to blood temperature

steps.text: Add dough ingredients to the breadmaker bowl, in the order recommended by the manufacturer.
Set the bread maker to the dough setting. While you wait, make the filling: with a fork or electric beaters, mix the butter, sugar and cinnamon together and set aside.
Tip the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Gently punch down the dough and knead lightly. Divide the dough into 2 even pieces.
Roll each piece into a large rectangle and spread each rectangle with half the filling mix.
Roll each piece into logs and cut each log into 12 slices with a sharp knife.
Place close together (optional) on a lined or greased baking tray/casserole dish. Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Cover the buns with cling wrap and allow to rise in a warm place for 20 minutes. (If you are making them for the next morning, cover with cling wrap and refrigerate until ready to bake.)
Bake for around 15–20 minutes or until well browned. Mix up the icing and drizzle over the warm buns.

recipes.title: Hot Cross Buns (Made with Breadmaker)
recipes.source: Recipe from recipetineats.com; glaze from taste.com.au

ingredients.heading: Buns
items: 50 g unsalted butter, melted and cooled

steps.text: Place bun ingredients into the breadmaker pan (except sultanas) in the order listed (according to machine guidelines). Add sultanas to the fruit and nut dispenser. Set machine to the dough setting.
Punch dough to deflate and place on a floured surface. Shape into a log. Cut into 12 equal pieces.
Form pieces into firm balls and place smooth side up on the baking tray (31.5 x 23.5 cm / 9 x 13 inch). Spray a piece of cling wrap with oil and place over tray.
Place tray in a warm place for 30–45 minutes, until the dough has risen by about 75%.
Preheat oven to 180 °C.

Crosses: mix flour and water until a thick, runny paste. Spoon into a round 3 mm piping bag or small ziplock bag, then snip the corner. Remove the cling wrap from the dough and pipe crosses onto the buns. Go slow so it hugs the curves.
Baking: bake in preheated oven (180 °C) for 22 minutes, or until the surface is a deep golden brown. The surface colour is the best test for this recipe.
Glaze: meanwhile, place water and sugar into a small saucepan over low heat. Stir until sugar dissolves. Bring to the boil. Boil for 3–4 minutes. Brush warm glaze over warm hot cross buns.

notes: Can use 2 cups of choc chips instead of sultanas (will melt in breadmaker, though).

recipes.title: Pancakes

steps.text: Measure ingredients into a fairly large bowl, in the order listed.
Beat with a whisk just until no longer lumpy. Do not overbeat or pancakes will be tough.
Heat frypan, then grease with butter.
Tip about 1/4 cup batter into pan, spreading to an even circle.
Turn pancake when bubbles break on the surface. Cook second side until the middle springs back when pressed with a finger.
Serve warm with toppings.

notes: Can freeze and reheat.

recipes.title: Best Pancake Recipe
recipes.source: Recipe by Test Kitchen (Women's Weekly Food)

items: 2 Tbsp melted butter, plus extra for brushing

steps.text: In a large bowl, combine flour and sugar. Make a well in the centre of the dry ingredients and whisk in egg, butter and vanilla.
Gradually whisk milk into mixture until a pouring consistency is achieved.

Heat a non-stick frying pan on medium. Brush pan with a little extra butter. Pour 1/4 cup of batter into pan to make a circle. Cook for 2–3 minutes or until bubbles start to appear on the surface. Turn and cook a further 1 minute until golden. Cover and keep warm. Repeat with remaining batter.
Melt butter, golden syrup and sugar together.
Add milk and beaten egg.
