Sift dry ingredients and mix all together.
Cook in a greased pan.

recipes.title: Pikelets (Women's Weekly)
recipes.source: Recipe by Test Kitchen (Women's Weekly Food)

items: Jam and whipped cream, to serve

steps.text: Sift flour and soda together into a medium bowl. Stir in sugar. Make a well in the centre. Gradually stir in egg and enough milk for a smooth pouring consistency. Rest 15 minutes.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan on medium. Brush with butter. Working in 3 batches of 6, drop tablespoons of batter into pan, allowing room for spreading. Cook 1–2 minutes, until bubbles appear on surface. Turn and cook 1 minute further, until golden. Brush pan with butter between batches.
Transfer cooked pikelets to a wire rack. Serve warm with jam and cream.
Stir the yeast, caster sugar and warm water together in a small bowl. Leave for 10 minutes until bubbling.
Mix the rice flour, plain flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well. Pour in the yeast mixture and mix to combine. Cover with plastic wrap and leave at room temperature for 3 hours.
Blitz the cinnamon, walnuts and brown sugar in a food processor until smooth.

Divide the dough into thirds and cut each third into 5 pieces. With lightly oiled hands, flatten each into a round about 10 cm across. Put 2 tsp of the walnut filling in the centre and seal the dough around it to make a small round cake.

Heat 4 Tbsp oil in a large deep-sided frying pan over medium heat. Add the hotteok and press down gently with an oiled spatula to flatten. Fry for 3–4 minutes until the edges start to brown (turning to cook both sides).
Serve warm.

items: Other flavourings: maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon

steps.text: Place 1/2 cup frozen berries (thawed) in a large bowl. Using a fork, crush lightly to release juices. Add oats, milk and 1/2 cup yoghurt, and stir. Cover and chill overnight.
Divide and serve with yoghurt, pepitas and extra berries if wanted.

recipes.title: Healthy Homemade Granola/Muesli

ingredients.heading: Dry ingredients
items: 1 cup raw nuts (e.g. sliced almonds, pecans, sunflower seeds, pepitas)
1 tsp favourite spice (cinnamon, a little ginger and mixed spice)

ingredients.heading: Wet ingredients
items: 1/3 cup sweetener (honey, maple syrup, brown sugar)
1/3 cup fat (coconut oil or melted butter)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 150 °C.
Combine dry ingredients except fruit (add brown sugar here if using).
Combine wet ingredients.
Combine wet and dry, then taste and adjust (i.e. more sweet/fat).
Spread on baking tray and bake until golden, approx. 35–40 minutes, tossing 2–3 times.
Stir through dried fruit. Cool. Store in an airtight container.

notes: Can also add soy protein with the fruit.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Muffins

ingredients.heading: Wet ingredients
items: 1 cup (250 ml) buttermilk (see note for substitute)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200 °C. Line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt in a bowl. Stir through choc chips.
In a separate bowl, whisk buttermilk, melted butter, oil, eggs and vanilla.
Make a well in the flour bowl and pour in egg mixture. Mix until just combined – try not to stir more than 8 times. Some flour lumps in the batter is fine.
Divide batter between paper cases. Top with remaining choc chips.
Bake for 5 minutes, then turn down to 180 °C and bake for a further 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Remove muffins from tin immediately onto a cooling rack.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Buttermilk substitute – combine 1 cup room-temperature whole milk + 1 tsp white vinegar. Let stand for 5 minutes until curdled, then use as per recipe.

items: 3/4 cup sour cream (or thick plain yoghurt)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 210 °C fan. Place shelf in top third of the oven. Line a 12-hole standard muffin tin with paper cases.
Sift dry ingredients: sift flour, baking soda and salt into a large bowl.
Bloom cocoa: in a separate bowl, sift the cocoa, then add coffee and hot milk. Whisk until lump-free.
Add remaining wet ingredients to the cocoa mixture (sugar, oil, egg, sour cream and vanilla). Whisk until smooth.
Mix flour in: pour wet mix into the bowl holding the flour. Whisk until smooth and glossy. Stop once it's smooth; don't mix excessively.
Add chocolate chips: stir in choc chips; can reserve some for topping.
Fill muffin tin: divide among 12 patty pans, up to 1/2 cm from rim.
Top with reserved chocolate chips.
Bake at high temperature for 5 minutes to kick-start the rise.
Lower the temperature to 190 °C and bake for a further 20 minutes (check at 15 minutes). When a toothpick comes out clean, they're ready.
Rest in muffin tin for a few minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack.
Filling: beat cream cheese and sugar together in a small bowl until light and fluffy.
In a large bowl, mix together sugar, flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt.
In a small bowl, combine milk, egg and oil.
Make a well in the centre of the dry ingredients and add the milk mixture.
Stir until just combined – don't overmix. (Add choc chips or nuts if wanted.)
Spoon 1 Tbsp of mixture into muffin pans. Drop 1 tsp cream cheese mixture on top and follow with another Tbsp of batter.
Bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes. Serve dusted with icing sugar.
Preheat oven to 220 °C.
With a fork, stir together dry ingredients in a large bowl.
In another bowl, melt butter, add milk, egg and vanilla and beat well.
Mash bananas and stir into the liquids.
Tip the liquids into the bowl with the dry ingredients.
Fold everything together carefully until all flour is dampened, but not overmixed.
Spray paper muffin cases. Half-fill to 3/4-fill muffin pans with mixture.
Bake at 220 °C for 12–15 minutes.

items: 1 cup vegetable oil (check for substitutes if you like)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 177 °C and prepare muffin tin.
Finely grate zucchini and gently wrap in a paper towel to squeeze out excess water.
In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, plus choc chips.
In a separate large bowl, add the bananas. Use a fork to mash. Add in the sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla. Stir well until fully combined.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Add zucchini and stir until incorporated.
Add 1/3 cup batter to each muffin hole. Bake for 22–26 minutes, or until an inserted toothpick is removed without wet batter. Tops should be rounded and golden brown.
Preheat oven to 177 °C. Line a muffin tin.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and soda, and salt until well combined.
In another bowl, whisk together the oil, milk, eggs, vanilla, sugar and brown sugar until smooth. Stir in the grated zucchini.
Add the wet mixture to the dry and stir until just combined.
Fold in choc chips.
Fill muffin tins 3/4 full and bake for 20–22 minutes.
Cool in tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Sieve the first 5 ingredients into a large bowl.
Melt butter, then add milk and egg and mix thoroughly.
Prepare fresh or frozen berries, then tip the liquid and fruit into the bowl with the dry mixture.
Fold everything together without overmixing.
Divide the mixture evenly into muffin pans.
Bake at 220 °C for 12–15 minutes, until muffins spring back when pressed. If using frozen berries, cook for an extra 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Apple and Zucchini Muffins

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Grease or line a 12-hole muffin pan.
In a medium bowl, combine flour, sugars and cinnamon.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs, oil and vanilla.
Stir in apple and zucchini.
Add in dry ingredients and stir to just combine.
Spoon into muffin pan.
Bake for 20–25 minutes.

notes: Banana may be used instead of apple.

steps.text: Mix flour, baking soda and sugar in a bowl.
Melt butter, add milk, egg and lemon rind and mix well.
Add liquids to the dry ingredients and combine only until dry ingredients have been lightly dampened.
Put mixture into muffin trays or paper pans sprayed with oil.
Bake at 200 °C for 10–15 minutes.
Stir together lemon juice and sugar and spoon over hot muffins.
Preheat oven to 210 °C.
Measure cheese and dry ingredients into a large bowl. Mix lightly to combine.
In a small container, beat the egg and milk until combined.
Pour liquid onto the dry ingredients, then fold the two mixtures together, taking care not to overmix.
Spoon mixture into 12 medium muffin pans which have been sprayed with non-stick spray.
Bake at 210 °C for about 12 minutes until cooked.

recipes.title: Mini Cinnamon Muffins
recipes.yield: Makes 24 mini muffins | Prep 20 mins | Cook 12 mins

items: 75 g unsalted butter, melted and cooled but still warm

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Mix the cinnamon sugar and set aside.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar vigorously for about 20 seconds until pale. Whisk in the oil, milk and vanilla.
Gently whisk in the flour in two lots, then the melted butter.
Spray a 24-hole mini muffin tin generously just before filling, and fill each hole three-quarters full.
Bake for 12 minutes. Cool 2 minutes, then turn out by tapping the tin firmly on the bench.
Toss the warm muffins in the cinnamon sugar and serve.

recipes.title: Morning Glory Muffins
recipes.source: Sally's Baking Addiction (sallysbakingaddiction.com) – method summarised; converted to °C
recipes.yield: Makes 14–16 muffins | Prep 30 mins | Cook 24 mins

items: 2 cups (260 g) wholemeal flour (spooned and levelled)
1/3 cup (80 ml) vegetable, canola or melted coconut oil
1/3 cup (80 g) unsweetened smooth apple sauce
1/3 cup (80 ml) orange or pineapple juice

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Grease or line a 12-hole muffin tin (you'll need a second tin or a second batch for the full amount).
Whisk the flour, bicarb, cinnamon, ginger, salt and flaxseed in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, sugar, honey, oil, apple sauce, zest, juice and vanilla, then whisk in the carrot and apple.
Pour the wet mix into the dry, stir a few times, add the raisins and pecans and fold until just combined with no dry pockets.
Fill the cases to the top. Bake 5 minutes at 220 °C, then reduce to 180 °C and bake about 18 minutes more, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin 10 minutes, then on a rack. Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or in the fridge for up to a week.
Preheat oven to 150 °C.
Cream butter and sugar together.
Add eggs and dry ingredients.
Add bananas and mix well. (Can add blueberries, cranberries, sultanas etc.)
Bake in a slow oven (150 °C) for 1 hour in a large loaf pan.

recipes.title: Fig Banana Bread

items: 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled

steps.text: Preheat oven to 176 °C. Grease loaf pan and line with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mash bananas with a fork until purée-like. Stir in melted butter until incorporated. Add in eggs and vanilla. Stir until well combined. Add brown sugar and mix until dissolved.
In a small bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon. Add to wet mixture. Fold to combine until there are no longer any dry streaks of flour.
Fold in chopped figs until well distributed. Transfer batter to prepared loaf pan. Arrange sliced figs on top. Sprinkle raw sugar, if desired.
Bake for 55–60 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the bread comes out clean. Allow bread to cool in pan for 10 minutes before unmoulding. Transfer bread to a wire rack to cool.

notes: Can add 1/2 cup toasted nuts. Best kept chilled.

steps.text: Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sift flours and salt, and add alternately with milk.
Add lemon rind.
Pour into a greased 20 x 10 cm loaf tin and bake at 180 °C for 40–45 minutes.
Mix lemon juice with extra sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves.
When cake is cooked and hot from the oven, pour over the lemon mixture.
Leave to cool in the tin.

recipes.title: Lemon Yoghurt Cake
recipes.source: Recipe from Donna Hay (there is also an alternative from Australia's Best Recipes)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 160 °C. Grease a 2.5 L bundt tin.
Place oil, eggs, lemon rind and juice, yoghurt and sugar in a large bowl and whisk to combine.
Sift in flour and whisk until smooth.
Pour into tin and bake for 50–55 minutes. Allow to cool in tin for 5 minutes.
Make icing – sift sugar, add lemon juice and water. Mix.
Carefully turn cake onto a plate. While cake is still hot, spoon over the icing. Allow to set for 10 minutes before slicing to serve.
Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Cream butter and sugar in a medium bowl.
Beat in condensed milk and cream until mixture is light and fluffy.
Stir flour and baking powder into butter mixture with chocolate chips.
Roll into balls and place on a lined oven tray. Flatten slightly with a fork.
Bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes or until bottoms are golden brown.

recipes.title: Alison Holst Crisp Choc Chip Cookies

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C.
Melt butter.
Add sugars and egg and mix well. Cool.
Add flour and baking soda and mix.
Add choc chips and mix in well.
Using a teaspoon, drop spoonfuls onto a tray lined with baking paper.
Leave plenty of room for spreading.
Bake for 8–10 minutes.
Cream together butter and sugars until light and fluffy. Whisk in egg and vanilla. Stir in flour and cocoa, then fold through chocolate chips.
Place teaspoonfuls on greased baking trays. Bake in a moderately slow oven (160 °C) for 10–15 minutes or until cooked. Cool on a wire rack.
Preheat oven to 150 °C.
Combine butter and golden syrup over gentle heat until melted (1 minute in the microwave).
Mix soda with boiling water and add to the butter mixture.
Put oats, flour, sugar and coconut in a bowl and combine.
Stir wet mix into dry ingredients.
Place spoonfuls of mixture onto a lined tray, allowing room for spreading.
Cook in a slow oven for 20 minutes.
Allow to cool on tray.

ingredients.heading: Cream filling
items: Vanilla or lemon essence, or passionfruit

steps.text: Cream butter, icing sugar and vanilla together until light and fluffy.
Add flour to cornflour and mix well.
Mix all ingredients together.
Put small balls on a lined tray and flatten with a fork.
Bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes.
Cool and join 2 together with cream filling.
Cream filling: cream butter with icing sugar. Flavour with vanilla or lemon essence, or passionfruit pulp.
Cream butter and sugar together.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Roll into balls and press down with a fork.
Bake in a slow oven, about 150 °C.
Put two together with chocolate icing (see recipe) when cool.

items: 1 cup oil OR 225 g melted butter

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C. Grease a 20–25 cm square pan, or use baking paper.
Combine oil/butter with sugar and vanilla.
Add eggs and mix well.
Add in flour, cocoa and baking powder and mix together until just combined.
Sprinkle choc chips/nuts etc. on bottom of pan and pour mixture over. Spread to edges.
Bake for 25–30 minutes.
Mix all ingredients together – add a little boiling water if too dry.
Press into a slice tin and bake at 180 °C for 10–15 minutes.
Can add cornflakes, sultanas, choc chips etc.
When cold, ice with chocolate icing (see recipe).
In a saucepan, melt butter, sugar and cocoa together. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Cool.
Add beaten egg and vanilla and whisk well together.
Add biscuits and sultanas and mix well.
Press into tin and refrigerate.
When set, ice with chocolate icing (see recipe) and decorate with nuts, sprinkles etc.

items: 180 g block milk chocolate, coarsely chopped
180 g block dark chocolate, coarsely chopped

steps.text: Grease and line a 22 cm square cake pan with baking paper.
Place condensed milk, milk chocolate and 100 g butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes or until melted and smooth.
Pulse biscuits and half the pretzels in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Stir into chocolate mixture until just combined, then stir in walnuts until combined.
Spoon mixture into prepared pan and level the surface. Refrigerate for 4 hours or until firm.

Place dark chocolate and remaining 40 g butter in a microwave-safe bowl and microwave on high for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until melted and smooth. Spread dark chocolate over top of slice. Top with remaining pretzels. Refrigerate for 1 hour or until dark chocolate sets. Cut into pieces to serve.

ingredients.heading: Base
items: Grated rind of 1 or 2 citrus fruits

steps.text: Melt the butter. Add condensed milk, coconut, grated rind and biscuit crumbs.
Mix together well, then press into a dish.
Mix icing ingredients together, adding just enough juice to make icing consistency.
Spread on top of base.
Refrigerate until firm.
Warm butter and condensed milk until melted together. Stir.
Add biscuit crumbs and fruit puffs. Mix all ingredients together.
Sprinkle coconut onto a piece of greaseproof paper and form a log from the mixture. Sprinkle with coconut.
Roll up and chill in the refrigerator.

items: 2/3 cup coconut, plus extra for rolling

steps.text: Crush biscuits and put in a bowl. Add cocoa, condensed milk and coconut.
Mix together well and roll into balls with damp hands.
Roll in coconut and set in the fridge.

items: 40 g dark chocolate, for top layer

steps.text: Soften dates by putting them in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, covered, and microwave for a bit. Mix well with a fork.
Blitz sunflower seeds in a food processor. Do the same with the Weet-Bix.
Combine all ingredients (except dark chocolate) in a bowl and mix well.
Press mixture into a tin lined with baking paper.
Melt dark chocolate and spread on top.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Slice. Store in fridge.

items: 1 cup dried fruit (e.g. currants, apricots, cranberries, sultanas, apple)

steps.text: Line a 20 x 30 cm slice tin with baking paper.
Warm the butter, coconut sugar and honey in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring now and then, until melted.
Mix all the dry ingredients in a large bowl, pour over the honey mixture and stir well.
Press firmly and evenly into the tin. Once slightly cooled, gently press the chocolate chips into the top.
Chill in the fridge or freezer for at least 1 hour, then cut into 18–20 bars.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
Put all pavlova ingredients into a mixer and beat until very stiff.
Bake in a preheated 175 °C oven for 15 minutes, then turn temperature down to 125 °C for 45 minutes.
When cooked, turn off oven and leave the pavlova in the oven to cool.
When cool, decorate with whipped cream and fruit or chocolate.
Whipped cream: beat cream, icing sugar and vanilla until just thickened.

recipes.title: Sticky Date Pudding with Butterscotch Sauce

ingredients.heading: Butterscotch sauce
items: To serve: ice cream or cream

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Grease 7 pudding moulds, or grease and line a 20 cm square cake tin with overhanging paper.
Put the dates in a bowl, sprinkle with bicarb and pour over the boiling water. Leave 10 minutes, then mash to a sloppy paste.
Beat the butter and sugar until smooth, then beat in the eggs. Add the flour, sprinkle over the baking powder and mix. Quickly mix in the dates.
One large pudding: pour into the tin and bake 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. While hot, poke about 40 holes over the top, pour over 1/2 cup sauce and leave 10 minutes to soak.
Individual puddings: fill the moulds two-thirds full and bake 25 minutes. Poke about 10 holes in each, spoon over 1 Tbsp sauce and soak 10 minutes, then turn out.
Sauce: put everything in a saucepan over medium heat. Once the butter melts, stir and simmer 2 minutes. Serve warm.
Serve the pudding warm with the remaining sauce and ice cream or cream.

ingredients.heading: Butterscotch sauce
items: 2 Tbsp cornflour (if your tablespoon is 20 ml, use 6 tsp)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and grease a 6-cup (1.6 L) baking dish.
Whisk the sauce sugar and cornflour together and set aside.
In another bowl, whisk the pudding sugar, flour and baking powder. Add the butter, egg, milk and golden syrup and whisk until mostly smooth.
Spread the batter in the dish and sprinkle the sauce sugar mixture evenly over the top.
Slowly pour the boiling water over, using the back of a spoon to soften the flow.
Bake 40 minutes, until a skewer in the cake part comes out clean.
Scoop into bowls, spoon over the sauce from underneath and serve with ice cream.

recipes.title: Golden Syrup Pudding (Microwave)

steps.text: In a bowl, mix together the sugar, flour, baking powder, eggs, milk and melted butter.
Put 3 Tbsp golden syrup in the bottom of a microwave bowl. Pour mixture on top of the golden syrup.
Cook covered in the microwave for 6–8 minutes.

notes: Can cook in a glass bowl with a dinner plate as a cover.

steps.text: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and cocoa together in a large bowl.
Then add the melted butter, milk and vanilla. Mix together well.
Put mixture into a microwave-proof bowl.
Sauce: mix the cocoa, sugar and boiling water. Pour slowly over the top of the pudding.
Cook in the microwave for 12 minutes.

items: Extras (optional): fresh berries or other fruit; Crunchie, chocolate; M&M's; nuts

steps.text: Beat cream with a mixer until it begins to thicken.
Add vanilla and beat until a light whipped cream forms.
Gradually add the condensed milk and keep beating until it thickens and becomes a nice cream.
Now is the time to add extra ingredients if you wish.
Pour into a container and freeze.

recipes.title: Ice Cream Sandwiches (Condensed Milk Ice Cream)

steps.text: Line a lamington tray with plastic wrap and place a layer of biscuits on top.
Whip condensed milk and cream together until thick. Fold through crumbled chocolate bar and spread mixture over biscuits.
Top with remaining biscuits.
Cover and freeze overnight. Cut into sections and serve.

items: 5 cups (900 g) fresh mango flesh (or tinned), roughly chopped

steps.text: Blend the mango and water until smooth, then push through a fine sieve – you need about 3 1/2 cups of purée.
Whisk the purée with the salt, sugar and lime juice until the sugar dissolves. Adjust sugar or lime to taste.
Churn in an ice-cream maker for 30 minutes.
Transfer to an airtight container and freeze for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.

items: 2 kg Granny Smith apples, cored, peeled, halved and sliced into 1 cm thick slices

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).
Mix the sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and salt in a bowl.
In a large bowl, sprinkle spice mix over apple slices. Toss well, separating pieces that are stuck together.
Spread apple across two large trays. Bake until soft but still holding form. Check first at 15 minutes, then frequently after that (may take up to 40 minutes). Do not stir or rotate trays.
Remove trays from oven. Using a spatula to hold the apples back, pour apple juices into a saucepan.
Leave apple slices to cool on the tray, about 15 minutes.
Apple syrup: add butter to apple juice saucepan and simmer on low heat until it reduces to 1/3 cup (80 ml), becoming syrupy. Remove from stove and let cool.
Pour apple syrup over slices when arranging pie.

items: 1 tsp popcorn salt (salt ground with mortar and pestle)

steps.text: Place 3 Tbsp ghee in a large 10 L lightweight pot over medium heat.
Add kernels and shake quickly to spread across the base, then clamp lid on. The kernels will start popping after a minute or so.
Shake briefly once after 30 seconds. When popping stops, immediately pour popcorn into a large bowl.
Melt extra ghee in microwave. Pour over popcorn and sprinkle over salt. Shake and toss to disperse.
Store in an airtight container for 2–3 days.
Soften 1 Tbsp butter in a bowl. Mix in about 2 cups icing sugar and about 1 Tbsp cocoa.
Slowly add in boiling water, about a teaspoon at a time, and mix to the right consistency.
Variations: Lemon icing – use lemon juice instead of water and leave out the cocoa. Peppermint – add peppermint essence etc.
Place all ingredients in a mixer/blender and mix for 3 minutes.
The mixture will be thin but thickens after an hour.
Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks or freeze extra.
